before.title: Adopted retarded solution selection: the physical branch carries no incoming free field
before.statement: Adopt as a physical assumption of this framework the following solution-selection rule for the classical vacuum model on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the constants and SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]] (so $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$). (a) [Formulation] In the potential formulation of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]] with the conventions of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], for a $C^2$ potential pair in Lorenz gauge the sourced Maxwell system of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] is equivalent to the decoupled sourced wave equations $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $WA=\mu_0J$, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$. The wave expression $W$ is invariant under $t\mapsto-t$; consequently, for a prescribed source history, the solution set of the sourced wave equations consists of one retarded branch (built from the retarded fundamental solution, support in the forward light cones) and one advanced branch, and the difference of any two solutions with the same source is a free field, i.e. a source-free solution of $W$. (b) [Adopted rule] The framework adopts the retarded branch with no free field added: the physical potential pair of the model is the retarded one, that is, the one whose support and propagation lie in the forward light cones of the source and which carries no field arriving from the past independently of the source. Equivalently: on any region for which initial data are prescribed on a spacelike Cauchy surface, the rule is that the homogeneous addition is exactly the one determined by those data, with zero incoming radiation; the advanced branch and every nonzero free field are excluded from the physical solution of this model. (c) [Status and scope] This is an adopted extra temporal condition carrying the model's arrow-of-time content. It is not a theorem, not a consequence of the time-symmetric wave or Maxwell equations (which admit advanced and free solutions as mathematical objects), and not a deduction from experiment; it asserts no existence, uniqueness, regularity, support or decay for any source class, all of which must be supplied separately by theorems of this page. It selects a solution only of the models to which it is applied; it introduces no product of distributions, no source model, no self-force, no radiation reaction, no measured signal and no statistical claim. The retarded compact-source branch to which this selection applies is developed on this page as a conditional theorem, and the point-source branch is developed later on this page; neither existence statement is part of this postulate.
before.strategy: A postulate: the item records an adopted solution-selection rule, and receives a source/scope review rather than a proof. The review checks that (i) the formulation correctly displays the wave expression $W$, its time-reversal symmetry, the retarded and advanced fundamental-solution branches and the free-field freedom, all with the exact interfaces of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]], [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]] and [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; (ii) the adopted rule is stated as a modelling choice with its arrow-of-time content, and is not presented as a consequence of the equations; (iii) the formulation does not pretend to prove existence or uniqueness for any source class and expressly defers those to the consuming theorems; (iv) no empirical, statistical, measurement or apparatus claim is made, and no quantitative precision is invented; and (v) the scope exclusions (advanced branch, free fields, arbitrary distributions, self-force) are explicit. The classical textbook treatments listed in the sources present the retarded/advanced distinction and the extra choice of the retarded Green function (Tong's 'extra choice' at the displayed page); they support the formulation and the honest status, and are not evidence for the physical correctness of the choice.
before.physical_scope: Adopted selection rule for the classical vacuum Maxwell/wave model in the framework's inertial laboratory chart and SI conventions: the physical potential pair is the retarded one with zero incoming free field. Excluded: existence, uniqueness, regularity or decay claims for any source class (consuming theorems must supply them); empirical, statistical or measurement claims; the advanced branch and free fields as physical solutions; products of distributions, self-force, radiation reaction and any apparatus model.

It is not a theorem, not a consequence of the time-symmetric wave or Maxwell equations (which admit advanced and free solutions as mathematical objects), and not a deduction from experiment; it asserts no existence, uniqueness, regularity, support or decay for any source class, all of which must be supplied separately by theorems of this page. before.title: Uniformly subluminal prescribed worldline, retarded root and retarded geometric data off the worldline
before.statement: Let the laboratory region, inertial chart, spatial Euclidean structure and SI units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], in particular $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. A **retarded point-geometry datum** consists of a real charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs ([[def-em-sources]](a)) and a prescribed map $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^3$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) together with a constant $0\le v_*<c$ such that $|z'(s)|\le v_*$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); the spacetime curve $s\mapsto(z(s),s)$ is the laboratory reading of a prescribed massive future timelike worldline of the physical model ([[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]), and $v_*$ is a declared bound on its coordinate speed, not a measured quantity. Write $\Gamma:=\{(z(s),s):s\in\mathbb R\}$ and $D:=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R:x\ne z(t)\}$ for the open off-worldline observation domain. Then: (a) [Retarded root] For every observation event $(x,t)\in D$ there is exactly one $s=s(x,t)<t$ with $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$; the map $s:D\to\mathbb R$ is of class $C^3$, and with the data of (b) below one has $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$ and $\nabla_xs=-n/(c\kappa)$ ([[lem-em-global-retarded-root]], whose $C^3$ branch applies because $z$ is $C^3$ and uniformly subluminal). (b) [Retarded data] For $(x,t)\in D$ define $R:=x-z(s(x,t))$, $r:=|R|>0$, $n:=R/r$, $\beta:=z'(s(x,t))/c$, $\kappa:=1-n\cdot\beta$, $\dot\beta:=z''(s(x,t))/c$; then $r=c(t-s)$ and $\kappa\in[1-v_*/c,\,1+v_*/c]\subseteq(0,\infty)$. On $D$ the objects $r$ and $n$ are of class $C^3$, $\beta$ and $\kappa$ are of class $C^2$, and $\dot\beta$ is of class $C^1$ (each is a composition of the $C^3$ root with $z$ or its derivatives). (c) [Emission-event data and emitted spheres] At an emission event $s_0\in\mathbb R$ and a direction $n\in S^2$ put $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$ for $r>0$, and $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\kappa_0:=1-n\cdot\beta_0$. Then $(x_r,t_r)\in D$ and $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$ for every $r>0$: the sphere $\{x_r\}$ at observation time $t_r$ is emitted at the single event $s_0$. (d) [Branches and scope] Only the all-time uniformly subluminal branch (a)-(c) is defined by this datum. For a curve prescribed on a finite interval $J$ the same formulas define retarded data only at observation events for which the root equation has a solution $s\in J$; each consumer must assume that cone intersection explicitly. Pointwise subluminality $|z'(s)|<c$ for every finite $s$ does not imply (a): the companion example on the examples page exhibits a smooth curve with $|z'|<c$ pointwise for which the retarded equation has no root at some event, so the uniform bound $v_*<c$, or an explicit cone-intersection hypothesis, is part of the datum. This definition is kinematic: it fixes the root, the retarded data and the notation, and asserts no field, no dynamics, no force law, no self-force and no empirical content. The identification of these data with the emission data of the physical field is made by the selection postulate [[post-em-radiation-selection]] together with the theorems of this page.
before.strategy: An explicit definition with its well-definedness discharged by a cited mathematical supplier. Existence, uniqueness and $C^3$ regularity of $s$ on $D$, together with $\kappa\in[1-v_*/c,1+v_*/c]$ and the derivative formulas, are exactly the all-time uniformly subluminal $C^3$ branch of [[lem-em-global-retarded-root]] (its statement covers every event of $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, hence every off-worldline event, and identifies equality $s=t$ with $x=z(t)$); no new analysis is needed, and the phrase 'prescribed worldline' is licensed by [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]](a),(c), which relates chart readings $t\mapsto r(t)$ of massive worldlines to the condition $|r'(t)|<c$. Clause (c) is the elementary root check $t_r-s_0=|x_r-z(s_0)|/c=r/c$ combined with the uniqueness in (a); no boundedness of $z''$ is used. Clause (d) records the branch boundaries honestly: the finite-history and nonuniform cases are left to consumers, and the failure of existence under mere pointwise subluminality is not asserted here but exhibited on the examples page. The definition introduces no physical field, so no Maxwell, self-force or empirical assertion is made; the cross-reference to the selection postulate records that the retarded root is the kinematic object that the adopted selection turns into an emission time. No choice principle beyond that carried by the cited root lemma is used.
before.physical_scope: Kinematic definition of the retarded emission data of a prescribed uniformly subluminal $C^3$ worldline in the framework's laboratory chart: retarded root, distance, direction, speed ratio and emission-time Jacobian off the worldline, and the emitted-sphere family. Excluded: any field, Maxwell equation, dynamics, force law, self-force, radiation reaction, existence under a merely pointwise subluminal or finite-history curve, and every empirical or measurement claim.

before.title: Uniform far-zone asymptotics and retarded-time flux limit for compact conserved smooth sources
before.statement:
Let $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $a>0$ and $t_0<T$ be constants, let $\rho\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R)$ and $\mathbf J\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R;\mathbb R^3)$ satisfy (H1) $\rho(y,v)=\mathbf J(y,v)=0$ whenever $|y|>a$ or $v\notin[t_0,T]$, and (H2) $\partial_v\rho+\operatorname{div}_y\mathbf J=0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$. For $x$ with $r:=|x|\ge2a$ define the retarded scalar and vector potentials $$\varphi(x,t):=\frac{\mu_0c^2}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\rho(y,t-|x-y|/c)}{|x-y|}\,dy,\qquad \mathbf A(x,t):=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\mathbf J(y,t-|x-y|/c)}{|x-y|}\,dy,$$ and the fields $\mathbf E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_t\mathbf A$, $\mathbf B:=\nabla\times\mathbf A$, where the derivatives are taken in $x$ and all objects are read on $\{|x|\ge2a\}$.

(a) (Fields as retarded integrals.) On the open set $\{|x|>2a\}$ the potentials $\varphi,\mathbf A$ are of class $C^\infty$ in $(x,t)$, and there $$\mathbf E(x,t)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Bigl[\frac{\mathbf N}{R^2}c^2\rho\bigl(y,t-\tfrac Rc\bigr)+\frac{\mathbf N}{cR}c\,\rho_t\bigl(y,t-\tfrac Rc\bigr)-\frac{\mathbf J_t\bigl(y,t-\tfrac Rc\bigr)}{R}\Bigr]dy,$$$$\mathbf B(x,t)=-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf N\times\Bigl[\frac{\mathbf J(y,t-\frac Rc)}{R^2}+\frac{\mathbf J_t(y,t-\frac Rc)}{cR}\Bigr]dy,$$ where $R:=|x-y|$, $\mathbf N:=(x-y)/R$, and $\rho_t,\mathbf J_t$ are the partial derivatives in the second variable. Moreover, on $\{|x|\ge2a\}\times[t_0,T]$, $\varphi$ and each component of $\mathbf A$ coincide with the corresponding solution constructed in the wave Cauchy problem of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] for zero Cauchy data at $t_0$ and scalar source $h=\mu_0c^2\rho$, respectively $h=\mu_0 J_k$.

(b) (Uniform far-zone expansion.) For $n\in S^2$ and $u\in[t_0,T]$ put $\mathbf I(n,u):=\int_{B_a}\mathbf J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$ and $\mathbf V(n,u):=\partial_u\mathbf I(n,u)=\int_{B_a}\mathbf J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$. Then $\int_{B_a}\rho_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy=\frac1c\,n\cdot\mathbf V(n,u)$, and there are constants $\Gamma_E,\Gamma_B$, depending only on $a,c,\mu_0$ and on the suprema of $|\rho|,|\rho_t|,|\rho_{tt}|,|\mathbf J|,|\mathbf J_t|,|\mathbf J_{tt}|$ on $\overline B_a\times[t_0,T]$, such that for every $n\in S^2$, $u\in[t_0,T]$ and $r\ge2a$, with $\mathbf E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r):=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times\mathbf V(n,u))$, $$\Bigl|\mathbf E(rn,u+\tfrac rc)-\mathbf E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2},\qquad \Bigl|\mathbf B(rn,u+\tfrac rc)-\frac{n\times\mathbf E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)}{c}\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}.$$

(c) (Retarded-time flux limit.) Let $\mathbf S:=\mu_0^{-1}\mathbf E\times\mathbf B$ and let $d\Omega$ be the surface measure on $S^2$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]). after.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the declared polar/surface and change-of-variables suppliers. Let $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $a>0$ and $t_0<T$ be constants, let $\rho\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R)$ and $\mathbf J\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R;\mathbb R^3)$ satisfy (H1) $\rho(y,v)=\mathbf J(y,v)=0$ whenever $|y|>a$ or $v\notin[t_0,T]$, and (H2) $\partial_v\rho+\operatorname{div}_y\mathbf J=0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$. For $x$ with $r:=|x|\ge2a$ define the retarded scalar and vector potentials $$\varphi(x,t):=\frac{\mu_0c^2}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\rho(y,t-|x-y|/c)}{|x-y|}\,dy,\qquad \mathbf A(x,t):=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\mathbf J(y,t-|x-y|/c)}{|x-y|}\,dy,$$ and the fields $\mathbf E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_t\mathbf A$, $\mathbf B:=\nabla\times\mathbf A$, where the derivatives are taken in $x$ and all objects are read on $\{|x|\ge2a\}$.

(b) (Uniform far-zone expansion.) (c) (Retarded-time flux limit.) Let $\mathbf S:=\mu_0^{-1}\mathbf E\times\mathbf B$ and let $d\Omega$ be the surface measure on $S^2$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]). Then for every $u\in[t_0,T]$, $$\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2\,n\cdot\mathbf S\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)\,d\Omega(n)=\frac{\mu_0}{16\pi^2c}\int_{S^2}\bigl|n\times\mathbf V(n,u)\bigr|^2\,d\Omega(n).$$ This is a limit at fixed retarded time $u$, not at fixed observation time $t$; no decay or boundary condition at spatial infinity is assumed beyond the compact spatial support in (H1).

before.title: Hypothesis boundaries: a causal response without passivity, and the fixed-retarded-time flux limit
before.reference: mathematical-example-verifications.md#ex-em-causal-response-and-radiation-prerequisites-hypothesis-boundaries; clause (ii) added by this scaffolder to exercise the second theorem's declared dependency (recorded in the batch notes)
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the surface-integral conventions used by [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]].

(i) (Causality without passivity.) In this clause also assume Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), inherited from the exact AC supplier. Let $K(s):=-e^{-s}$ for $s\ge0$. Then $K$ is of class $C^1$ on $[0,\infty)$ with $K,K'\in L^1(0,\infty)$ and $sK(s)\in L^1(0,\infty)$ (indeed $K'=e^{-s}=-K$, $\int_0^\infty e^{-s}ds=1$ and $\int_0^\infty se^{-s}ds=1$), so the integrable branch of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]] applies: $P(t)=\int_0^\infty K(s)E(t-s)ds$ is a bounded causal linear response on bounded continuous histories, its transfer function is $\chi(z)=-1/(1-iz)$ on $\operatorname{Im}z\ge0$, and its boundary value $\chi(\omega)=-(1+i\omega)/(1+\omega^2)$ satisfies $\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)=-\omega/(1+\omega^2)<0$ for every $\omega>0$. Hence the Hermitian dissipative part $M(\omega)=\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)$ is strictly negative, not positive semidefinite, and the monochromatic period-averaged work of clause (d) of that theorem is strictly negative for $d=1$, every $e\ne0$ and every $\omega>0$ (with any response normalization $\varepsilon_0>0$), although the response is causal and its entry satisfies the dispersion relations of clause (c). Nonnegative period-averaged work (passivity) is therefore an additional condition on the model, not a consequence of temporal causality.

(ii) (The flux limit needs fixed retarded time.) In the setting of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]], fix $t\in\mathbb R$ and $n\in S^2$, and let $r>\max\{2a,\;a+c(t-t_0)\}$. Then for every $y\in B_a$ one has $R=|rn-y|\ge r-a>c(t-t_0)$, so $t-R/c<t_0$; by hypothesis (H1) of that theorem the functions $\rho,\rho_t,\mathbf J,\mathbf J_t$ all vanish at $(y,t-R/c)$, so every integrand in the field formulas of clause (a) of that theorem vanishes and $\mathbf E(rn,t)=\mathbf B(rn,t)=0$, hence $n\cdot\mathbf S(rn,t)=0$ for every $n\in S^2$. Therefore $\int_{S^2}r^2\,n\cdot\mathbf S(rn,t)\,d\Omega(n)=0$ for all such $r$: at fixed observation time the far-zone flux integral is identically zero beyond the light cone of the compact spacetime support, whereas clause (c) of that theorem is a limit at fixed retarded time. The retarded-time formulation cannot be replaced by a fixed-observation-time one.
before.strategy:
Proof technique: direct computation and direct substitution into the two cited theorems.

(i) The real exponential is differentiable with $\exp'=\exp$ ([[thm-derivative-of-exponential]], [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]]) and $\exp(-s)>0$ with $\exp(-s)=1/\exp(s)$ ([[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]]), so $s\mapsto K(s)=-e^{-s}$ is of class $C^1$ on $[0,\infty)$ with $K'=e^{-s}=-K$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). For every $N>0$ the Newton-Leibniz formula gives $\int_0^Ne^{-s}ds=1-e^{-N}$ and integration by parts (with $u=s$, $v=-e^{-s}$) gives $\int_0^Nse^{-s}ds=1-(1+N)e^{-N}$ ([[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]], [[thm-integration-by-parts]]); the continuous real integrands have the same Lebesgue integrals by [[thm-bounded-riemann-integrable-functions-are-lebesgue-measurable-and-have-the-same-integral]]; [[thm-c1-lipschitz-ac-bv-hierarchy]] proves the explicit $C^1$ kernel is absolutely continuous on each compact interval in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]]; the displayed Newton-Leibniz integral representations agree with the Lebesgue FTC under this regularity. Thus it has the absolute-continuity property required by the integrable branch of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]], and passing to the limit with monotone convergence for the nonnegative integrands gives $\int_0^\infty e^{-s}ds=\int_0^\infty se^{-s}ds=1$, so $K,K',sK(s)\in L^1(0,\infty)$ ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]], [[def-l-one-of-a-measure]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]). Clause (a) of the theorem therefore gives the bounded causal response. For the transfer function, fix real $\omega$; the complex exponential is entire with derivative itself and the complex chain rule gives that $s\mapsto F(s)=\exp((-1+i\omega)s)/(-1+i\omega)$ is a primitive of $s\mapsto\exp((-1+i\omega)s)$ on $\mathbb C$ ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-complex-derivatives]], [[def-complex-exponential]]), so the fundamental theorem for complex line integrals along the interval path $[0,N]\ni s\mapsto s$ gives $\int_{[0,N]}\exp((-1+i\omega)s)\,ds=F(N)-F(0)$ ([[thm-fundamental-theorem-for-complex-line-integrals]], [[def-complex-primitive]], [[def-complex-line-integral-over-a-rectifiable-path]], [[thm-riemann-stieltjes-and-parametric-contour-integrals-agree]]). Hence $\int_0^N(-e^{-s})e^{i\omega s}ds=-(F(N)-F(0))$, and $\left|e^{(-1+i\omega)N}\right|=e^{-N}\to0$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]); letting $N\to\infty$ with dominated convergence for the integrands dominated by $e^{-s}$ gives $\chi(\omega)=-1/(1-i\omega)$, and the same computation with $z$ in place of $\omega$ gives $\chi(z)=-1/(1-iz)$ for $\operatorname{Im}z>0$ ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]). Taking real and imaginary parts ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) gives $\chi(\omega)=-(1+i\omega)/(1+\omega^2)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)=-\omega/(1+\omega^2)<0$ because $\omega>0$. With $d=1$, $e=1$ and $\varepsilon_0>0$, clause (d) of the theorem gives period-averaged work $\frac{\varepsilon_0\omega}{2}\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)<0$ and $M(\omega)=\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)<0$, so the passivity condition fails while causality holds: this witnesses the logical independence recorded in the theorem's proof discussion.

(ii) For $y\in B_a$ the reverse triangle inequality gives $R=|rn-y|\ge r-a>c(t-t_0)$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), hence $t-R/c<t_0$ and all four source functions vanish at the arguments appearing in the field integrals of clause (a) of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]]; each integrand is identically zero on $B_a$, so $\mathbf E(rn,t)=\mathbf B(rn,t)=0$ and therefore $n\cdot\mathbf S(rn,t)=\mu_0^{-1}n\cdot(\mathbf E\times\mathbf B)(rn,t)=0$ for every $n\in S^2$. after.title: Hypothesis boundaries: a causal response without passivity, and the fixed-retarded-time flux limit
after.reference: mathematical-example-verifications.md#ex-em-causal-response-and-radiation-prerequisites-hypothesis-boundaries; clause (ii) added by this scaffolder to exercise the second theorem's declared dependency (recorded in the batch notes)
after.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the surface-integral conventions used by [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]].

(i) (Causality without passivity.) In this clause also assume Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), inherited from the exact AC supplier. Let $K(s):=-e^{-s}$ for $s\ge0$. Then $K$ is of class $C^1$ on $[0,\infty)$ with $K,K'\in L^1(0,\infty)$ and $sK(s)\in L^1(0,\infty)$ (indeed $K'=e^{-s}=-K$, $\int_0^\infty e^{-s}ds=1$ and $\int_0^\infty se^{-s}ds=1$), so the integrable branch of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]] applies: $P(t)=\int_0^\infty K(s)E(t-s)ds$ is a bounded causal linear response on bounded continuous histories, its transfer function is $\chi(z)=-1/(1-iz)$ on $\operatorname{Im}z\ge0$, and its boundary value $\chi(\omega)=-(1+i\omega)/(1+\omega^2)$ satisfies $\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)=-\omega/(1+\omega^2)<0$ for every $\omega>0$. Hence the Hermitian dissipative part $M(\omega)=\operatorname{Im}\chi(\omega)$ is strictly negative, not positive semidefinite, and the monochromatic period-averaged work of clause (d) of that theorem is strictly negative for $d=1$, every $e\ne0$ and every $\omega>0$ (with any response normalization $\varepsilon_0>0$), although the response is causal and its entry satisfies the dispersion relations of clause (c). Nonnegative period-averaged work (passivity) is therefore an additional condition on the model, not a consequence of temporal causality.

(ii) (The flux limit needs fixed retarded time.) In the setting of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]], fix $t\in\mathbb R$ and $n\in S^2$, and let $r>\max\{2a,\;a+c(t-t_0)\}$. Then for every $y\in B_a$ one has $R=|rn-y|\ge r-a>c(t-t_0)$, so $t-R/c<t_0$; by hypothesis (H1) of that theorem the functions $\rho,\rho_t,\mathbf J,\mathbf J_t$ all vanish at $(y,t-R/c)$, so every integrand in the field formulas of clause (a) of that theorem vanishes and $\mathbf E(rn,t)=\mathbf B(rn,t)=0$, hence $n\cdot\mathbf S(rn,t)=0$ for every $n\in S^2$. Therefore $\int_{S^2}r^2\,n\cdot\mathbf S(rn,t)\,d\Omega(n)=0$ for all such $r$: at fixed observation time the far-zone flux integral is identically zero beyond the light cone of the compact spacetime support, whereas clause (c) of that theorem is a limit at fixed retarded time. The retarded-time formulation cannot be replaced by a fixed-observation-time one.
after.strategy:
Proof technique: direct computation and direct substitution into the two cited theorems.

(i) The real exponential is differentiable with $\exp'=\exp$ ([[thm-derivative-of-exponential]], [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]]) and $\exp(-s)>0$ with $\exp(-s)=1/\exp(s)$ ([[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]]), so $s\mapsto K(s)=-e^{-s}$ is of class $C^1$ on $[0,\infty)$ with $K'=e^{-s}=-K$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). before.title: The retarded wave kernel is a distribution supported on the cone, solves the point-wave equation, and convolves to the retarded solution
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), used through the sphere and polar integrations below ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]]). Let $c>0$, write $Q:=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, $\mathcal D:=\mathcal D(Q)$ for the test-function space of [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], and $C:=\{(y,t)\in Q:t=|y|/c\}$ for the retarded cone. Define the functional $K$ on test functions by $$\langle K,\psi\rangle:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\psi(y,|y|/c)}{|y|}\,dy\qquad(\psi\in\mathcal D).$$ Then: (a) the integral converges absolutely for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$, the functional $K$ is a distribution on $Q$ ([[def-distribution]]), $(K,\psi)=0$ for every $\psi$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\cap C=\varnothing$, and for every $(y_0,t_0)\in C$ and every neighbourhood $U$ of $(y_0,t_0)$ there is $\psi\in\mathcal D$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\subseteq U$ and $\langle K,\psi\rangle\ne0$; consequently $\operatorname{supp}K=C$. (b) For every $h\in C_c^\infty(Q)$ the function $$(K*h)(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{h(y,\,t-|x-y|/c)}{4\pi\,|x-y|}\,dy$$ is well defined (the integral converges absolutely), of class $C^\infty$ on $Q$, and for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$ $$\langle K*h,\psi\rangle=\langle h,\,K\circledast\psi\rangle,\qquad (K\circledast\psi)(y,s):=\langle K,\psi(y+\cdot,s+\cdot)\rangle=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int\frac{\psi(y+z,s+|z|/c)}{|z|}\,dz;$$ moreover $W(K*h)=h$ on $Q$ in the classical pointwise sense, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ is the wave expression of [[def-wave-equation-cauchy-data-and-wave-speed]] and [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]. (c) Read $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ as the distributional operator built from [[def-distributional-derivative]]; then $WK=\delta_{(0,0)}$ in the sense of [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]], that is, $(WK)(\psi)=\psi(0,0)$ for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$. This identifies $K$ as the retarded fundamental solution of $W$; no smoothness of $K$ itself on the cone is asserted, and the advanced fundamental solution is not treated.
before.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) Well-definedness and continuity: fix $\psi\in\mathcal D$ with support in a compact set, choose $R>0$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\subseteq B_R(0)\times[-R,R]$ ([[thm-heine-borel-rn]]), and let $M:=\sup|\psi|<\infty$ on the compact support ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]]). Then $|\langle K,\psi\rangle|\le\frac{M}{4\pi}\int_{B_R}|y|^{-1}dy$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]), and by [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] applied to the nonnegative Borel function $y\mapsto|y|^{-1}\mathbf 1_{B_R}(y)$, with $d\sigma$ the polar measure of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], $\int_{B_R}|y|^{-1}dy=\int_0^Rr^{-1}\sigma(S^2)r^2\,dr=\tfrac12\sigma(S^2)R^2<\infty$. Hence the integral converges absolutely and the bound is a fixed-support seminorm of [[def-fixed-support-test-function-frechet-space]] on each $\mathcal D_K$, i.e. $K$ is continuous for the LF topology of [[def-test-function-topology]]: $K\in\mathcal D'$. Support: if $\operatorname{supp}\psi\cap C=\varnothing$ then $\psi(y,|y|/c)=0$ for every $y\ne0$, so the integrand vanishes off the null set $\{0\}$ and $\langle K,\psi\rangle=0$. Conversely fix $(y_0,t_0)\in C$ and a neighbourhood $U$. If $y_0\ne0$, take a nonnegative bump $\psi$ supported in a small ball inside $U$ about $(y_0,t_0)$ with $\psi(y_0,t_0)>0$: by continuity $\psi(\cdot,|\cdot|/c)$ is positive on a neighbourhood of $y_0$, a set of positive measure, and $|y|^{-1}$ is bounded there, so $\langle K,\psi\rangle>0$ ([[thm-nonnegative-integral-zero-iff-zero-almost-everywhere]], [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]). If $y_0=0$, then $t_0=0$ and $\psi(y,t)=\rho(|y|)\eta(t)$ with nonnegative bump factors supported in a small ball about the origin inside $U$ and positive at the origin gives $\langle K,\psi\rangle=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int\rho(|y|)\eta(|y|/c)|y|^{-1}dy>0$ by the same positivity argument. Hence no point of $C$ is outside the support and $\operatorname{supp}K=C$. (b) For fixed $(x,t)$ the defining integral converges absolutely: if $\operatorname{supp}h\subseteq\overline B_\rho(0)\times[-\rho,\rho]$ and $(y,t-|x-y|/c)\in\operatorname{supp}h$, then $y\in\overline B_{\rho+|x|}(0)$; $|h|\le\|h\|_\infty$ and $1/(4\pi|x-y|)$ is integrable over that compact ball by the same polar computation, so [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]] gives absolute convergence. Pairing identity: substitute $x=y+z$ in the $x$-integral and $t=s+|z|/c$ in the $t$-integral (two translations of Lebesgue measure, [[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]]) and interchange the $y$- and $(z,t)$-integrations with [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] (the integrand is continuous on the compact product of the supports): $\langle K*h,\psi\rangle=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int h(y,s)\Bigl[\int\frac{\psi(y+z,s+|z|/c)}{|z|}dz\Bigr]dyds=\langle h,K\circledast\psi\rangle$, the inner bracket being exactly the definition of $K$ applied to the test function $(z,u)\mapsto\psi(y+z,s+u)$ (its support is compact). Identification with the wave solution: let $h\in C_c^\infty(Q)$ and $t_0$ below the time support of $h$. Apply [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] with $a=b=0$ and source $h$ on the slab $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$, $T$ above the time support: its solution is $u(x,t)=c^2\int_{t_0}^tH_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$ with $H_\varphi(x,s)=sM_{cs}\varphi(x)$, $M_{r}\varphi(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}\varphi(x+rn)\,d\Omega(n)$. Writing the sphere average as an integral over the sphere and using [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] on the compact rectangle $[t_0,t]\times S^2$, the substitution $r=c(t-v)$ with the absolute derivative ([[cor-one-dimensional-change-of-variables-with-absolute-derivative]]) turns the integral into $u(x,t)=\int_0^{c(t-t_0)}r\,\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}h(x+rn,t-r/c)\,d\Omega(n)\,dr$. The chart surface measure on $S^2$ agrees with the polar measure $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], $n=3$), so applying [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] to the nonnegative Borel function $y\mapsto|h(x+y,t-|y|/c)|(4\pi|y|)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{|y|\le c(t-t_0)}$ (and passing to positive and negative parts, [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]) gives $u(x,t)=\int_{|y|\le c(t-t_0)}\frac{h(x+y,\,t-|y|/c)}{4\pi|y|}\,dy$; the omitted range $|y|>c(t-t_0)$ has $t-|y|/c<t_0$, where $h=0$. After the reflection $y\mapsto-y$ this is $(K*h)(x,t)$ on the whole slab. Since for every point $(x_*,t_*)\in Q$ one can choose a slab $[t_0,T]$ containing it with $t_0$ below and $T$ above the time support of $h$, [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] gives $Wu=h$ at that point and $K*h=u$ there; hence $K*h$ (well defined on all of $Q$ and smooth on every slab) is $C^\infty$ on $Q$ and $W(K*h)=h$ pointwise. (c) Let $\eta\in C_c^\infty(Q)$ be a nonnegative bump with $\int\eta=1$ and $\operatorname{supp}\eta\subseteq\overline B_1(0)$ and let $\eta_\varepsilon$ be its mollifier family ([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]], [[def-l-one-approximate-identity-on-rn]]). By (b), $W(K*\eta_\varepsilon)=\eta_\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. For bounded continuous $\varphi$, $\langle\eta_\varepsilon,\varphi\rangle\to\varphi(0)$: convolve with the reflected bump and apply [[cor-l-one-approximate-identities-converge-uniformly-on-compacta-for-continuous-functions]] at the origin. Hence for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$, $\langle K*\eta_\varepsilon,\psi\rangle=\langle\eta_\varepsilon,K\circledast\psi\rangle\to(K\circledast\psi)(0,0)=\langle K,\psi\rangle$, because $K\circledast\psi$ is continuous (its defining integral is dominated by $2\|\psi\|_\infty/(4\pi|z|)$ on a compact $z$-set, so [[thm-dominated-convergence]] applies as $(y,s)\to(0,0)$), i.e. $K*\eta_\varepsilon\to K$ in the weak topology of $\mathcal D'$. The distributional operator $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ is a continuous linear map on $\mathcal D'$ for the weak topology, being a finite linear combination of derivatives, each of which is continuous linear ([[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); therefore $WK=W(\lim_\varepsilon K*\eta_\varepsilon)=\lim_\varepsilon W(K*\eta_\varepsilon)=\lim_\varepsilon\eta_\varepsilon=\delta_{(0,0)}$ in $\mathcal D'$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]). No smoothness of $K$ on the cone is claimed or used.

Pairing identity: substitute $x=y+z$ in the $x$-integral and $t=s+|z|/c$ in the $t$-integral (two translations of Lebesgue measure, [[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]]) and interchange the $y$- and $(z,t)$-integrations with [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] (absolute integrability follows by bounding h and psi and enclosing the contributing y,s,z in a bounded cylinder; the only pole is 1/|z|, whose integral over a bounded ball is finite by the preceding polar calculation; continuity at the pole is neither true nor required): $\langle K*h,\psi\rangle=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int h(y,s)\Bigl[\int\frac{\psi(y+z,s+|z|/c)}{|z|}dz\Bigr]dyds=\langle h,K\circledast\psi\rangle$, the inner bracket being exactly the definition of $K$ applied to the test function $(z,u)\mapsto\psi(y+z,s+u)$ (its support is compact). Identification with the wave solution: let $h\in C_c^\infty(Q)$ and $t_0$ below the time support of $h$. Apply [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] with $a=b=0$ and source $h$ on the slab $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$, $T$ above the time support: its solution is $u(x,t)=c^2\int_{t_0}^tH_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$ with $H_\varphi(x,s)=sM_{cs}\varphi(x)$, $M_{r}\varphi(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}\varphi(x+rn)\,d\Omega(n)$. Writing the sphere average as an integral over the sphere and using [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] on the compact rectangle $[t_0,t]\times S^2$, the substitution $r=c(t-v)$ with the absolute derivative ([[cor-one-dimensional-change-of-variables-with-absolute-derivative]]) turns the integral into $u(x,t)=\int_0^{c(t-t_0)}r\,\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}h(x+rn,t-r/c)\,d\Omega(n)\,dr$. The chart surface measure on $S^2$ agrees with the polar measure $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], $n=3$), so applying [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] to the nonnegative Borel function $y\mapsto|h(x+y,t-|y|/c)|(4\pi|y|)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{|y|\le c(t-t_0)}$ (and passing to positive and negative parts, [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]) gives $u(x,t)=\int_{|y|\le c(t-t_0)}\frac{h(x+y,\,t-|y|/c)}{4\pi|y|}\,dy$; the omitted range $|y|>c(t-t_0)$ has $t-|y|/c<t_0$, where $h=0$. After the reflection $y\mapsto-y$ this is $(K*h)(x,t)$ on the whole slab. Since for every point $(x_*,t_*)\in Q$ one can choose a slab $[t_0,T]$ containing it with $t_0$ below and $T$ above the time support of $h$, [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] gives $Wu=h$ at that point and $K*h=u$ there; hence $K*h$ (well defined on all of $Q$ and smooth on every slab) is $C^\infty$ on $Q$ and $W(K*h)=h$ pointwise. (c) Let $\eta\in C_c^\infty(Q)$ be a nonnegative bump with $\int\eta=1$ and $\operatorname{supp}\eta\subseteq\overline B_1(0)$ and let $\eta_\varepsilon$ be its mollifier family ([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]], [[def-l-one-approximate-identity-on-rn]]). By (b), $W(K*\eta_\varepsilon)=\eta_\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. For bounded continuous $\varphi$, $\langle\eta_\varepsilon,\varphi\rangle\to\varphi(0)$: convolve with the reflected bump and apply [[cor-l-one-approximate-identities-converge-uniformly-on-compacta-for-continuous-functions]] at the origin. Hence for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$, $\langle K*\eta_\varepsilon,\psi\rangle=\langle\eta_\varepsilon,K\circledast\psi\rangle\to(K\circledast\psi)(0,0)=\langle K,\psi\rangle$, because $K\circledast\psi$ is continuous (its defining integral is dominated by $2\|\psi\|_\infty/(4\pi|z|)$ on a compact $z$-set, so [[thm-dominated-convergence]] applies as $(y,s)\to(0,0)$), i.e. $K*\eta_\varepsilon\to K$ in the weak topology of $\mathcal D'$. The distributional operator $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ is a continuous linear map on $\mathcal D'$ for the weak topology, being a finite linear combination of derivatives, each of which is continuous linear ([[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); therefore $WK=W(\lim_\varepsilon K*\eta_\varepsilon)=\lim_\varepsilon W(K*\eta_\varepsilon)=\lim_\varepsilon\eta_\varepsilon=\delta_{(0,0)}$ in $\mathcal D'$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]). No smoothness of $K$ on the cone is claimed or used. For the approximate-identity application in (c), F(y,s)=(K circledast psi)(y,s) is bounded on ALL parameter space: if the spatial projection of supp psi lies in B_M with M>0, the contributing z lie in B_M-y. For |y|<=2M this is contained in B_3M and its |z|^-1 integral is finite; for |y|>2M one has |z|>=|y|-M>M and the integral is bounded by |B_M|/M. Multiply by ||psi||infinity/(4pi). Continuity on every bounded parameter neighborhood follows from the same fixed compact-z polar majorant and dominated convergence. Thus the stated bounded-continuous approximate-identity interface is actually applicable.

before.title: Retarded Liénard-Wiechert potentials and fields of a uniformly subluminal smooth point source
before.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $c>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$, $\varepsilon_0>0$, put $\mu_0:=(c^2\varepsilon_0)^{-1}$ and $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$, and let $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ be of class $C^3$ with $|z'(s)|\le v_*<c$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]). Write $\Omega:=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ and $\Gamma:=\{(z(s),s):s\in\mathbb R\}\subseteq\Omega$. For $(x,t)\in\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ let $s=s(x,t)$ be the unique retarded root of [[lem-em-global-retarded-root]] with $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$, and put $R:=x-z(s)$, $r:=|R|>0$, $n:=R/r$, $\beta:=z'(s)/c$, $\kappa:=1-n\cdot\beta$, $N:=n\cdot\beta$, $D:=\kappa r$, $\dot\beta:=z''(s)/c$ and $d:=n\cdot\dot\beta$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then: (a) the distributions $\rho,J\in\mathcal D'(\Omega)$ of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]], $$\langle\rho,\psi\rangle=q\int_{\mathbb R}\psi(z(s),s)\,ds,\qquad \langle J,\psi\rangle=q\int_{\mathbb R}z'(s)\,\psi(z(s),s)\,ds,$$ satisfy $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. (b) Let $K$ be the retarded wave kernel of [[lem-em-retarded-wave-kernel]] and, for $\psi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ and $\tau\in\mathbb R$, $y\in\mathbb R^3$, put $(K\circledast\psi)(y,\tau):=\langle K,\psi(y+\cdot,\tau+\cdot)\rangle$. Define the retarded-history pairings by the explicit integrals
$$\langle\Phi,\psi\rangle:=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\int_{\mathbb R}(K\circledast\psi)(z(s),s)\,ds,\qquad
\langle\Upsilon,\psi\rangle:=\mu_0q\int_{\mathbb R}z'(s)(K\circledast\psi)(z(s),s)\,ds.$$
Here the second integral is componentwise. The notation $\varepsilon_0^{-1}\langle\rho,K\circledast\psi\rangle$ and $\mu_0\langle J,K\circledast\psi\rangle$, if used, means precisely these explicit history integrals, rather than ordinary distribution action on a compactly supported test. These pairings define distributions on $\Omega$, are finite for every $\psi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ and satisfy the exact retarded-convolution identities $$\langle\Phi,\psi\rangle=\int_{\Omega\setminus\Gamma}\frac{C\,\psi(x,t)}{\kappa(x,t)\,r(x,t)}\,dx\,dt,\qquad \langle\Upsilon,\psi\rangle=\int_{\Omega\setminus\Gamma}\frac{\beta(x,t)}{c}\,\frac{C\,\psi(x,t)}{\kappa(x,t)\,r(x,t)}\,dx\,dt$$ (for $\Upsilon$, componentwise against $\psi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$; both integrands are continuous on the open set $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ and integrable there against $\psi$). Consequently the potentials are the $C^2$ functions $$\varphi:=\frac{C}{D}=\frac{C}{\kappa r}:\Omega\setminus\Gamma\to\mathbb R,\qquad A:=\frac{\beta\,\varphi}{c}=\frac{\beta\,C}{c\,\kappa r}:\Omega\setminus\Gamma\to\mathbb R^3$$ off the worldline, and the zero extensions $\widetilde\varphi,\widetilde A$ on $\Gamma$ belong to $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$; $\Phi$ is the regular distribution of $\widetilde\varphi$, and $\Upsilon$ that of $\widetilde A$ ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function|regular distribution]]). (c) Let $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B:=\operatorname{curl}A$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]). Then, off the worldline, $$E=C\left[\frac{(1-|\beta|^2)(n-\beta)}{\kappa^3r^2}+\frac{n\times\bigl((n-\beta)\times\dot\beta\bigr)}{c\,\kappa^3r}\right],\qquad B=\frac{n\times E}{c}.$$ The fields $E,B$ are $C^1$ off the worldline. More generally, if $z\in C^k$, $k\ge3$, the retarded root is $C^k$, the potentials are $C^{k-1}$ and the fields are $C^{k-2}$ there; if $z\in C^\infty$, all these objects are smooth off the worldline. The result is a mathematical model computation for the stipulated uniformly subluminal smooth worldline and the retarded choice; no self-force law, no radiation-reaction postulate and no physical Maxwell coupling is asserted or proved.
before.strategy:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as stipulated in the statement. (a) Apply [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] to the $C^1$ curve $z$ on $\mathbb R$; $C^3$ is a special case, and its all-time graph is proper because a compact ambient set bounds the time coordinate.
(b) Fix a compact observation set $Q\subseteq\{(x,t):|x|\le M,\ t_0\le t\le t_1\}$, and tests supported in $Q$. If $g(s,y):=(z(s)+y,s+|y|/c)\in Q$, then $s\le t_1$. For $s\le0$, using $|z(s)|\le Z+v_*|s|$ with $Z:=|z(0)|$ gives
$$t_0\le s+|y|/c=s+|x-z(s)|/c\le -(1-v_*/c)|s|+(M+Z)/c.$$
Thus $s\ge-S$, where $S:=\max\{0,(M+Z-ct_0)/(c-v_*)\}$. If $[-S,t_1]$ is empty no contributing point exists. Otherwise set $H:=\max(S,|t_1|)$ and $L:=1+M+Z+v_*H$. Every contributing $y$ has $|y|\le M+|z(s)|<L$. Consequently the pulled-back support lies in the bounded closed cylinder $[-S,t_1]\times\overline B_L$, possibly approaching $y=0$; it need not be compact inside $U:=\mathbb R\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$.
On that cylinder, $|\psi(g(s,y))|/(4\pi|y|)\le\|\psi\|_\infty/(4\pi|y|)$. The polar formula [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] gives $\int_{B_L}|y|^{-1}dy=\sigma(S^2)L^2/2<\infty$. Borel product identification [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]] and the Euclidean/product-measure bridge [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]] allow [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] for the absolute value. Then [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] identifies the double integral with the explicit iterated history integral. In particular, with $T:=\max(0,t_1+S)$ and $M_Q:=T\sigma(S^2)L^2/(8\pi)$,
$$|\langle\Phi,\psi\rangle|\le |q|M_Q\|\psi\|_\infty/\varepsilon_0,\qquad
|\langle\Upsilon_j,\psi\rangle|\le\mu_0|q|v_*M_Q\|\psi\|_\infty.$$
The seminorm $\psi\mapsto|\langle\Phi,\psi\rangle|$ restricts continuously to each fixed-support test space by these bounds, and likewise for each component of $\Upsilon$. Thus [[def-test-function-topology]] and [[def-distribution]] prove distribution continuity directly; no action of $\rho$ or $J$ on a noncompact test is assumed.
The graph $\Gamma$ is closed: convergence of $(z(s_j),s_j)$ forces $s_j\to t$ and $z(s_j)\to z(t)$. Thus $V:=\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ is open. On $U$, $g$ is $C^1$, and in coordinate order $(s,y_1,y_2,y_3)$ its determinant is $-\kappa(s,y)$, with $\kappa=1-(y/|y|)\cdot z'(s)/c\ge1-v_*/c>0$. If $g(s,y)=g(s',y')$, then $|s-s'|=||y'|-|y||/c\le|z(s')-z(s)|/c\le(v_*/c)|s-s'|$, so $s=s'$ and $y=y'$. No image point belongs to $\Gamma$: otherwise $|y|=|z(t)-z(s)|\le v_*(t-s)=v_*|y|/c$, contradicting $y\ne0$. Conversely every point of $V$ has the unique retarded root supplied by [[lem-em-global-retarded-root]], giving inverse $(x,t)\mapsto(s(x,t),x-z(s(x,t)))$. Its $C^1$ regularity follows from that supplier's $C^3$ branch on the open domain $x\ne z(t)$, using this consumer's $C^3$ hypothesis. No exclusion of the entire spatial trajectory is imposed. Therefore $g:U\to V$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism.
For any compact $Q\subseteq\Omega$, the nonnegative Borel substitution lemma [[lem-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-borel-functions-via-radon-uniqueness]] applied to $1_Q/(\kappa r)$ on $V$ yields
$$\int_V\frac{1_Q}{\kappa r}\,dx\,dt=\int_U\frac{1_Q(g(s,y))}{|y|}\,ds\,dy<\infty.$$
The same bound holds for $|\beta|/(c\kappa r)$ since $|\beta|\le v_*/c$. Extend the potentials by zero on the closed graph. These extensions are Borel and locally integrable on all of $\Omega$. Applying the same Borel substitution first to the absolute value of $\psi/(\kappa r)$ establishes its $L^1$ integrability on $V$, and [[cor-c-one-change-of-variables-for-l-one-functions]] then gives the scalar pairing formula in the statement. Apply it componentwise to $z'(s)$-weighted data for the vector formula. Its prefactor is
$$\frac{\mu_0qz'(s)}{4\pi\kappa r}=\frac{\mu_0qc\beta}{4\pi\kappa r}=\frac{\mu_0c\varepsilon_0 C\beta}{\kappa r}=\frac{C\beta}{c\kappa r},$$
since $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$. The regular-distribution identities mean the zero extensions, as in [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]; tests may be nonzero on $\Gamma$. The retarded root is $C^3$ on $V$, and $r,n$ are $C^3$ while $\beta,\kappa,D$ are $C^2$ with $D>0$, so the potentials are $C^2$. The same composition argument gives the matching $C^k$ and $C^\infty$ branches.
(c) Derivatives of the retarded data: from $t-s=r/c$ and R1, $\nabla s=-n/(c\kappa)$, $s_t=1/\kappa$, hence $\nabla r=n/\kappa$ and $r_t=-cN/\kappa$ (chain rule, [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]); $R=x-z(s)$ gives $\partial_iR=e_i+\beta\,n_i/\kappa$ and $\beta=z'(s)/c$ gives $\partial_i\beta=-\dot\beta\,n_i/(c\kappa)$, while $\beta_t=\dot\beta/\kappa$ (componentwise chain rule and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]). Since $D=r-R\cdot\beta$, the product rules for the Euclidean pairing give $D_t=r_t-R_t\cdot\beta-R\cdot\beta_t=(c(|\beta|^2-N)-rd)/\kappa$ and $\partial_iD=\partial_ir-(\partial_iR)\cdot\beta-R\cdot\partial_i\beta$, hence $\nabla D=((1-|\beta|^2+rd/c)/\kappa)\,n-\beta$; the required product rules are the coordinatewise one-variable product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then $\varphi=C/D$ gives $\nabla\varphi=-C\nabla D/D^2$, $\varphi_t=-CD_t/D^2$, and $A=\beta\varphi/c$ gives $A_t=(\beta_t\varphi+\beta\varphi_t)/c=\dot\beta C/(c\kappa D)-\beta CD_t/(cD^2)$, so $$E=-\nabla\varphi-A_t=\frac{C}{D^2}\Bigl(\nabla D+\frac{\beta D_t}{c}\Bigr)-\frac{C\dot\beta}{c\kappa D}.$$ The bracket equals $\frac{(1-|\beta|^2)(n-\beta)+(rd/c)(n-\beta)}{\kappa}$ (substituting the two displayed identities and $\kappa=1-N$), and writing the second term over the common denominator $\kappa^3r^2$ replaces its numerator by $-r\kappa\dot\beta/c$, giving $E=\frac{C}{\kappa^3r^2}\bigl[(1-|\beta|^2)(n-\beta)+\frac{r}{c}\bigl(d(n-\beta)-\kappa\dot\beta\bigr)\bigr]$; the coordinate triple-product identity $n\times((n-\beta)\times\dot\beta)=d(n-\beta)-\kappa\dot\beta$ (expand both sides with [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]) yields the displayed $E$. For the magnetic field, $\operatorname{curl}(\beta\varphi/c)=\nabla(\varphi/c)\times\beta+(\varphi/c)\operatorname{curl}\beta$ ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]), and $\operatorname{curl}\beta=\nabla s\times\dot\beta$ by the coordinate formula applied to $\beta=z'(s(x,t))/c$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]); substituting $\nabla\varphi=-C\nabla D/D^2$ and $\nabla s=-n/(c\kappa)$ gives $$B=-C\left[\frac{1-|\beta|^2+rd/c}{c\kappa D^2}\,n\times\beta+\frac{n\times\dot\beta}{c^2\kappa D}\right].$$ Crossing the displayed $E$ with $n/c$ gives this same expression by $n\times(n-\beta)=-n\times\beta$ and $D=\kappa r$, proving $B=n\times E/c$. Both displayed fields are $C^1$ off the worldline, and no derivative of $z$ beyond the third order and no bound on $\Gamma$ at infinity is used; the caveats in the statement are exactly those of the research branch argument.

(b) Fix a compact observation set $Q\subseteq\{(x,t):|x|\le M,\ t_0\le t\le t_1\}$, and tests supported in $Q$. If $g(s,y):=(z(s)+y,s+|y|/c)\in Q$, then $s\le t_1$. For $s\le0$, using $|z(s)|\le Z+v_*|s|$ with $Z:=|z(0)|$ gives
$$t_0\le s+|y|/c=s+|x-z(s)|/c\le -(1-v_*/c)|s|+(M+Z)/c.$$
Thus $s\ge-S$, where $S:=\max\{0,(M+Z-ct_0)/(c-v_*)\}$. If $[-S,t_1]$ is empty no contributing point exists. Otherwise set $H:=\max(S,|t_1|)$ and $L:=1+M+Z+v_*H$. Every contributing $y$ has $|y|\le M+|z(s)|<L$. Consequently the pulled-back support lies in the bounded closed cylinder $[-S,t_1]\times\overline B_L$, possibly approaching $y=0$; it need not be compact inside $U:=\mathbb R\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$.
On that cylinder, $|\psi(g(s,y))|/(4\pi|y|)\le\|\psi\|_\infty/(4\pi|y|)$. The polar formula [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] gives $\int_{B_L}|y|^{-1}dy=\sigma(S^2)L^2/2<\infty$. Borel product identification [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]] and the Euclidean/product-measure bridge [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]] allow [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] for the absolute value. Then [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] identifies the double integral with the explicit iterated history integral. In particular, with $T:=\max(0,t_1+S)$ and $M_Q:=T\sigma(S^2)L^2/(8\pi)$,
$$|\langle\Phi,\psi\rangle|\le |q|M_Q\|\psi\|_\infty/\varepsilon_0,\qquad
|\langle\Upsilon_j,\psi\rangle|\le\mu_0|q|v_*M_Q\|\psi\|_\infty.$$
The seminorm $\psi\mapsto|\langle\Phi,\psi\rangle|$ restricts continuously to each fixed-support test space by these bounds, and likewise for each component of $\Upsilon$. Thus [[def-test-function-topology]] and [[def-distribution]] prove distribution continuity directly; no action of $\rho$ or $J$ on a noncompact test is assumed.
The graph $\Gamma$ is closed: convergence of $(z(s_j),s_j)$ forces $s_j\to t$ and $z(s_j)\to z(t)$. Thus $V:=\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ is open. before.reference: batch-21-local-construction (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-21.notes.md); the design reserves no example for this B page, and this example checks lem-em-retarded-wave-kernel(a), lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability(b)-(c) and lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields(c) in explicit instances
before.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (i) Static specialization. Take $z\equiv0$ (so $v_*=0$), $q\in\mathbb R$, $\varepsilon_0>0$, in the setting of [[lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields]]. Then for $x\ne0$ the root is $s=t-|x|/c$, $r=|x|$, $n=x/|x|$, $\beta=0$, $\kappa=1$, $\dot\beta=0$, so the potentials and fields are $\varphi=C/|x|$, $A=0$, $E=C\,x/|x|^3$, $B=0$. Thus the retarded formulas reduce exactly to the Coulomb field with the convention $C=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$, and the kernel's explicit retarded-history integral reproduces the time-independent Poisson kernel $1/(4\pi|x-y|)$: for a static spatial source $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, define the all-time retarded extension by
$$u(x,t):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{h(y)}{|x-y|}\,dy.$$
Indeed the retarded time is $t-|x-y|/c$ and evaluating the static source there leaves $h(y)$ unchanged. This finite integral is the extension of the compact spacetime-source formula by source-time cutoffs on each compact observation region; a time-independent nonzero source is not itself compactly supported in spacetime. (ii) Explicit Lorenz-gauge transformation. On $\Omega=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ take $\varphi\equiv0$ and $A(x,t)=(x_1,0,0)$. Then $G(\varphi,A)=\operatorname{div}A=1$ and $E=-\partial_tA=0$, $B=\operatorname{curl}A=0$. The quadratic function $\chi(x,t):=-|x|^2/6$ satisfies $W\chi=G$: indeed $\partial_t^2\chi=0$ and $\Delta\chi=-1$, so $W\chi=c^{-2}\cdot0-(-1)=1=G$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]). Its gauge transform is $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(0,\ ((2/3)x_1,-x_2/3,-x_3/3))$, which satisfies $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=\frac23-\frac13-\frac13=0$ and has the same fields: $E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=0=E(\varphi,A)$ and $B(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=0=B(\varphi,A)$. This checks clauses (b) and (c) of [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] in an instance where $G$ is a nonzero constant and where the gauge function does not have the zero Cauchy data used in the existence construction of that lemma; by its clause (d), the difference of this $\chi$ and the zero-data solution of $W\chi=G$ solves the homogeneous wave equation, which is why both may be used. (iii) Sharpness of the kernel support at the apex. For a nonnegative $\psi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R)$ with $\psi(0,0)>0$ one has $\langle K,\psi\rangle=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int\psi(y,|y|/c)|y|^{-1}dy>0$, so $(0,0)\in\operatorname{supp}K$ and the apex is not an artefact of the definition; the same computation with a bump near $(y_0,|y_0|/c)$, $y_0\ne0$, shows that every point of the cone is in the support. These are mathematical checks of the pair's conventions and hypotheses; no measurement, physical field identification, or empirical claim is made.

before.title: Retarded potentials, Lorenz gauge and Maxwell fields of a compactly supported conserved smooth source
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the retarded-kernel and Cauchy suppliers below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], so that $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ is the wave expression of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]. Let $a>0$, $t_0<T$ and let $ho:\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R	o\mathbb R$, $J:\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R	o\mathbb R^3$ be source fields of [[def-em-sources]] that are jointly of class $C^\infty$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], vanish identically outside the compact set $\overline B_a(0)	imes[t_0,T]$, and satisfy the continuity equation $\partial_tho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ everywhere -- the compatibility condition that [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] shows to be forced by the Maxwell system, here assumed for the prescribed source. Define the retarded potentials by the explicit retarded integrals $$\varphi(x,t):= rac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3} rac{ho igl(y,t-|x-y|/c igr)}{|x-y|}\,dy,\qquad A(x,t):= rac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3} rac{J igl(y,t-|x-y|/c igr)}{|x-y|}\,dy,$$ and put $E:=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=
abla	imes A$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]). Then: (a) [Smoothness and wave equations] $\varphi$ and each component of $A$ are of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$, and $W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0$, $WA=\mu_0J$ pointwise. (b) [Lorenz gauge] With $G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$ one has $G=0$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$: the retarded pair is in Lorenz gauge, and this is exactly where the continuity hypothesis is used. (c) [Maxwell fields] $E$ and $B$ are of class $C^\infty$ and the tuple $(E,B,ho,J)$ satisfies the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the whole of $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$: $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $
abla	imes E=-\partial_tB$, $
abla	imes B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. (d) [No field before the source] $E=B=0$ at every event with $t<t_0$ (indeed $\varphi=A=0$ there): the selected retarded solution carries no field from before the source acted. (e) [Zero-data Cauchy identification] For every $t_1<t_0$ the pair $(\varphi,A)$ restricted to $\mathbb R^3	imes[t_1,\infty)$ is the unique $C^2$ extension solution of the wave Cauchy problem of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] at time $t_1$ with zero Cauchy data and sources $ho/\varepsilon_0$, $\mu_0J$. (f) [Total charge] The total charge $Q(t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}ho(y,t)\,dy$ is zero for every $t$: a source that is smooth, compactly supported in space and restricted to a compact time interval and satisfies continuity carries zero total charge, so this branch does not model an eternal isolated nonzero charge. (g) [Scope] This is the compact smooth branch with an adopted causal selection; it asserts nothing about point, line or sheet sources, about weak or distributional branches, about finite-energy or decay properties, about radiation reaction or self-force, and no empirical claim. In particular the fields of a prescribed isolated point charge with an eternal worldline are not covered by this theorem and are supplied separately by the point-source items of this page.
before.strategy:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) $ho,J$ are $C^\infty$ with compact support, hence $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R)$; clause (b) of [[lem-em-retarded-wave-kernel]] applied to $h=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and componentwise to $h=\mu_0J_k$ states that $(K*h)(x,t)=\int h(y,t-|x-y|/c)/(4\pi|x-y|)dy$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$ and satisfies $W(K*h)=h$ pointwise, which is exactly the display. Note the identification $\varphi=\varepsilon_0^{-1}K*ho$, $A=\mu_0K*J$ is the framework's form of the adopted retarded selection of [[post-em-radiation-selection]]; the selected branch is the object being computed, not assumed to exist a priori. (b) Differentiate the explicit retarded integral. In the substitution $y'=x-y$, which leaves the integral unchanged by translation invariance of Lebesgue measure ([[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]]), the kernel $1/(4\pi|y'|)$ is independent of $x$, so differentiating under the integral sign in $x$ ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]], applicable because the integrand is smooth and compactly supported in $y$ for $(x,t)$ in a bounded set) gives $\partial_{x^i}(K*h)=K*(\partial_{y^i}h)$; differentiating in $t$ gives $\partial_t(K*h)=K*(\partial_th)$. Therefore $\operatorname{div}A=\mu_0K*(\operatorname{div}J)$ and $c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi=c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}K*(\partial_tho)=\mu_0K*(\partial_tho)$ because $c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}=\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0\cdot\varepsilon_0^{-1}c^{-2}$ reduces to $\mu_0$ (equivalently $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$, [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Adding, $G=\mu_0K*(\partial_tho+\operatorname{div}J)=0$ by the assumed continuity. (c) $\varphi,A$ are $C^\infty$, hence $C^2$, and clause (a) of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]] (instantiated at $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$) states the exact identities $\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG$ and $
abla	imes B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+
abla G$; with (a) and (b) these read $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and $
abla	imes B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J$. The two source-free equations $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $
abla	imes E+\partial_tB=0$ are automatic for a potential pair by the curl-divergence and curl-gradient cancellation recorded in clause (c) of the same item and [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]. This is the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. (d) If $t<t_0$ then for every $y$ the retarded argument satisfies $t-|x-y|/c\le t<t_0$, where $ho$ and $J$ vanish; both integrands vanish identically, so $\varphi(x,t)=A(x,t)=0$ and hence $E=B=0$ at such events. (e) Fix $t_1<t_0$. By (d), $\varphi(\cdot,t_1)=0$ and $\partial_t\varphi(\cdot,t_1)=0$, and likewise for $A$; by (a) the pair is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes[t_1,\infty)$ and solves the sourced wave equations there. Clause (b) of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] (uniqueness for $C^2$ extension solutions of the Cauchy problem with these data) identifies the pair with its zero-data solution; clause (d) of the same theorem gives the corresponding finite-speed support, consistent with (d). (f) $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\partial_tho(y,t)dy=-\int_{\mathbb R^3}\operatorname{div}J(y,t)dy=0$: for a ball $B_R$ with $R>a$ the divergence theorem ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]]) converts the integral of $\operatorname{div}J$ into a boundary flux where $J=0$, and differentiation under the integral sign is licensed by compact support ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]]); hence $Q$ is constant, and $Q(t)=0$ for $t<t_0$ by (d), so $Q\equiv0$. (g) records the branch boundaries. No self-force, no product of distributions and no empirical premise is used; the only choice assumption is $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, inherited from the kernel and Cauchy suppliers through the surface-measure and convergence interfaces cited inside them.
before.physical_scope: Retarded potentials and fields of a prescribed smooth conserved source of compact spatial support in a compact time interval, on the whole laboratory spacetime in the framework's inertial chart: Lorenz gauge, the smooth vacuum Maxwell equations, zero field before the source acts, the zero-data Cauchy identification and zero total charge. Excluded: point, line, sheet or non-integrable sources; weak/distributional branches; eternal isolated charges; finite-energy, decay or boundary claims; self-force and radiation reaction; and every empirical or measurement claim.

before.title: Zonal and quadratic sphere moments for the polar surface measure on $S^2$
before.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the dipole and emitted-power items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-36.notes.md)
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), as carried by the surface-measure interface below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on the unit sphere $S^2\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), let $e_3$ be the third vector of the standard basis and write $n_3=n\cdot e_3$ for $n\in S^2$. Then: (a) [Zonal identity] for every continuous $f:[-1,1]\to\mathbb R$, $$\int_{S^2}f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du.$$ (b) [Linear weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)\,f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3\int_{-1}^{1}u\,f(u)\,du.$$ (c) [Quadratic weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3^{2}\int_{-1}^{1}u^{2}f(u)\,du+\pi\,(a_1^{2}+a_2^{2})\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})f(u)\,du.$$ (d) [Moments] $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$, $\int_{S^2}n\,d\sigma=0$, $\int_{S^2}n_in_j\,d\sigma=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$, and for every $a\in\mathbb R^3$ $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$ and $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker symbol and $\times$ the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (e) [Scope] (a)-(d) are identities for the polar surface measure of the unit sphere with only the stated continuity of $f$; they assert no physical field, flux or radiation statement. The measure is finite, so all displayed integrals are absolutely convergent; $f$ need not be nonnegative. For the uses on this page $f$ is a rational function with denominator bounded below by $1-b>0$, hence continuous on $[-1,1]$.
before.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) Parametrize $S^2$ by $X(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta)$ on $[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$. Computing the coordinate cross product with the sin/cos derivatives and the Pythagorean identity ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) gives $X_\theta\times X_\varphi=\sin\theta\,X(\theta,\varphi)$, whose norm is $\sin\theta\ge0$; by [[thm-surface-area-density-is-cross-product-norm]] and [[def-surface-area-and-scalar-surface-integral-of-a-patch]] the chart surface integral of $F(n)=f(n_3)$ is $\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi$, with the seam and the poles lying on the parameter boundary exactly as in the sphere-area computation, so this is the integral over $S^2$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-parameter-boundary-exceptions-do-not-affect-surface-integrals|the boundary-exception convention]]). The chart measure equals the polar measure $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). By [[thm-jordan-fubini-by-sections]] the $\varphi$-integral is the constant $2\pi$, and with $P(u):=\int_0^u f$ ([[thm-ftc-first-part]]) the chain rule and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta=[-P(\cos\theta)]_0^{\pi}=P(1)-P(-1)=\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du$, using $\cos0=1$, $\cos\pi=-1$ and the derivative $\cos'=-\sin$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]). This proves (a), including the endpoint values by continuity of $P\circ\cos$ on $[0,\pi]$ and the two-sided fundamental theorem. (b) Write $n\cdot a=a_1n_1+a_2n_2+a_3n_3$. The maps $\eta_1(n_1,n_2,n_3):=(-n_1,n_2,n_3)$ and $\eta_2(n_1,n_2,n_3):=(n_1,-n_2,n_3)$ are orthogonal and preserve $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]); since $n_1f(n_3)$ and $n_2f(n_3)$ change sign under $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ respectively, the substitution formula for the measure-preserving involution $\eta_i$ (indicators by definition, simple functions by linearity, bounded Borel functions by the usual approximation, exactly as in the vanishing-first-moment computation of [[lem-first-moment-of-the-unit-sphere-vanishes]]) gives $\int n_if(n_3)d\sigma=-\int n_if(n_3)d\sigma=0$ for $i=1,2$; the remaining term is $a_3\int n_3f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi a_3\int_{-1}^1uf(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=uf(u)$. (c) Expanding the square, the mixed terms $n_in_jf(n_3)$ with $i\ne j$ vanish by the same reflection argument; the terms $n_1^2$ and $n_2^2$ are equal by the swap $(n_1,n_2,n_3)\mapsto(n_2,n_1,n_3)$, which is orthogonal and preserves $\sigma$. Hence $\int n_1^2f(n_3)d\sigma=\int n_2^2f(n_3)d\sigma=\tfrac12\int(1-n_3^2)f(n_3)d\sigma=\pi\int_{-1}^1(1-u^2)f(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=(1-u^2)f(u)$, while $\int n_3^2f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi\int_{-1}^1u^2f(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=u^2f(u)$; linearity of the $\sigma$-integral on the (finite-measure) integrable functions is [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]. This proves (c). (d) Taking $f=1$ in (a) gives $\sigma(S^2)=2\pi\cdot2=4\pi$, which also evaluates the closed form of [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]] at $n=3$ together with the Gamma values $\Gamma(5/2)=(3/2)(1/2)\Gamma(1/2)=3\sqrt\pi/4$ ([[thm-real-gamma-functional-equation]], [[cor-real-gamma-one-half-is-root-pi]]), so the two routes agree. after.title: Zonal and quadratic sphere moments for the polar surface measure on $S^2$

after.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), as carried by the surface-measure interface below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on the unit sphere $S^2\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), let $e_3:=(0,0,1)$ be the third coordinate unit vector and write $n_3=n\cdot e_3$ for $n\in S^2$. Then: (a) [Zonal identity] for every continuous $f:[-1,1]\to\mathbb R$, $$\int_{S^2}f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du.$$ (b) [Linear weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)\,f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3\int_{-1}^{1}u\,f(u)\,du.$$ (c) [Quadratic weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3^{2}\int_{-1}^{1}u^{2}f(u)\,du+\pi\,(a_1^{2}+a_2^{2})\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})f(u)\,du.$$ (d) [Moments] $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$, $\int_{S^2}n\,d\sigma=0$, $\int_{S^2}n_in_j\,d\sigma=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$, and for every $a\in\mathbb R^3$ $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$ and $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker symbol and $\times$ the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (e) [Scope] (a)-(d) are identities for the polar surface measure of the unit sphere with only the stated continuity of $f$; they assert no physical field, flux or radiation statement. The measure is finite, so all displayed integrals are absolutely convergent; $f$ need not be nonnegative. For the uses on this page $f$ is a rational function with denominator bounded below by $1-b>0$, hence continuous on $[-1,1]$.
after.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) Parametrize $S^2$ by $X(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta)$ on $[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$. Computing the coordinate cross product with the sin/cos derivatives and the Pythagorean identity ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) gives $X_\theta\times X_\varphi=\sin\theta\,X(\theta,\varphi)$, whose norm is $\sin\theta\ge0$; by [[thm-surface-area-density-is-cross-product-norm]] and [[def-surface-area-and-scalar-surface-integral-of-a-patch]] the chart surface integral of $F(n)=f(n_3)$ is $\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi$, with the seam and the poles lying on the parameter boundary exactly as in the sphere-area computation, so this is the integral over $S^2$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-parameter-boundary-exceptions-do-not-affect-surface-integrals|the boundary-exception convention]]). The chart measure equals the polar measure $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). By [[thm-jordan-fubini-by-sections]] the $\varphi$-integral is the constant $2\pi$, and with $P(u):=\int_0^u f$ ([[thm-ftc-first-part]]) the chain rule and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta=[-P(\cos\theta)]_0^{\pi}=P(1)-P(-1)=\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du$, using $\cos0=1$, $\cos\pi=-1$ and the derivative $\cos'=-\sin$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]). This proves (a), including the endpoint values by continuity of $P\circ\cos$ on $[0,\pi]$ and the two-sided fundamental theorem. (b) Write $n\cdot a=a_1n_1+a_2n_2+a_3n_3$. The maps $\eta_1(n_1,n_2,n_3):=(-n_1,n_2,n_3)$ and $\eta_2(n_1,n_2,n_3):=(n_1,-n_2,n_3)$ are orthogonal and preserve $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]); since $n_1f(n_3)$ and $n_2f(n_3)$ change sign under $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ respectively, the substitution formula for the measure-preserving involution $\eta_i$ (indicators by definition, simple functions by linearity, bounded Borel functions by the usual approximation, exactly as in the vanishing-first-moment computation of [[lem-first-moment-of-the-unit-sphere-vanishes]]) gives $\int n_if(n_3)d\sigma=-\int n_if(n_3)d\sigma=0$ for $i=1,2$; the remaining term is $a_3\int n_3f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi a_3\int_{-1}^1uf(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=uf(u)$. (c) Expanding the square, the mixed terms $n_in_jf(n_3)$ with $i\ne j$ vanish by the same reflection argument; the terms $n_1^2$ and $n_2^2$ are equal by the swap $(n_1,n_2,n_3)\mapsto(n_2,n_1,n_3)$, which is orthogonal and preserves $\sigma$. Hence $\int n_1^2f(n_3)d\sigma=\int n_2^2f(n_3)d\sigma=\tfrac12\int(1-n_3^2)f(n_3)d\sigma=\pi\int_{-1}^1(1-u^2)f(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=(1-u^2)f(u)$, while $\int n_3^2f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi\int_{-1}^1u^2f(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=u^2f(u)$; linearity of the $\sigma$-integral on the (finite-measure) integrable functions is [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]. This proves (c). (d) Taking $f=1$ in (a) gives $\sigma(S^2)=2\pi\cdot2=4\pi$, which also evaluates the closed form of [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]] at $n=3$ together with the Gamma values $\Gamma(5/2)=(3/2)(1/2)\Gamma(1/2)=3\sqrt\pi/4$ ([[thm-real-gamma-functional-equation]], [[cor-real-gamma-one-half-is-root-pi]]), so the two routes agree. Finally $|n\times a|^2=|a|^2-(n\cdot a)^2$ by the cross-product norm identity ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), so $\int|n\times a|^2d\sigma=4\pi|a|^2-(4\pi/3)|a|^2=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$. Clause (e) records that no physical interpretation is attached. No choice principle beyond $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ (carried by the surface-measure interface) is used.
