before.title: Controlled electric-dipole far field and retarded-time radiated power of a compact smooth source
before.statement: Assume the setting and hypotheses of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by its suppliers: $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $a>0$, $t_0<T$, jointly $C^\infty$ fields $\rho,J$ vanishing outside $\overline B_a(0)\times[t_0,T]$ and satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$; let $\varphi,A$ be the retarded potentials and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\nabla\times A$ the fields, with $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Adopt the causal selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]]: these retarded fields are the fields of the source model (the compact smooth instance established by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]). Define the **time-dependent electric dipole moment** $$p(u):=\int_{B_a}y\,\rho(y,u)\,dy\in\mathbb R^3$$ (componentwise, about the fixed chart origin of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; it is the fixed-time analogue of the static source moment of [[def-em-electric-moments]]), and, as in the asymptotic theorem, $I(n,u):=\int_{B_a}J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$, $V(n,u):=\partial_uI(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$ and $$D(u):=\frac{a}{c}\int_{B_a}\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|\,dy.$$ Then: (a) [Moment identities] $p\in C^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^3)$, $p'(u)=\int_{B_a}J(y,u)\,dy$, $p''(u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u)\,dy$, $\int_{B_a}\rho_t(y,u)\,dy=0$ and the total charge $\int_{B_a}\rho(y,u)\,dy$ vanishes for every $u$. (b) [Dipole replacement error] $|V(n,u)-p''(u)|\le D(u)$ for every $n\in S^2$ and every $u\in[t_0,T]$: the explicit absolute error of the dipole approximation to the source's transverse current moment. (c) [Leading fields] With $\Gamma_E$, $\Gamma_B$ the constants of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](b) (depending only on $a,c,\mu_0$ and the listed source suprema), for every $n\in S^2$, $u\in[t_0,T]$, $r\ge2a$: $$\Bigl|E\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p''(u))\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0D(u)}{4\pi r},\qquad \Bigl|B\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{n\times E(rn,u+\tfrac rc)}{c}\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}.$$ The leading far field is the electric-dipole field, with amplitude proportional to $p''(u)$; all errors are uniform in the direction $n$ at fixed $u$. (d) [Retarded-time radiated power] The limit of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](c) equals $\mu_0|p''(u)|^2/(6\pi c)+R(u)$ with the explicit absolute error $$|R(u)|\le\frac{\mu_0\bigl(2|p''(u)|D(u)+D(u)^2\bigr)}{4\pi c},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)d\sigma=\frac{\mu_0}{6\pi c}|p''(u)|^2\ \text{ exactly when } D(u)=0.$$ The evaluation uses the sphere moment $\int_{S^2}|n\times p''|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|p''|^2$ of [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d). The limit is at fixed retarded time $u$, not at fixed observation time. (e) [Scope] The compact smooth source branch only; the dipole error is absolute and explicitly controlled by $D(u)$, and no assertion is made that slow or 'nonrelativistic' source motion alone makes $D(u)$ small -- that is a hypothesis on the source's time variation. No point charge, no moving point source, no radiation reaction, no self-force and no empirical or measurement content; the failure of the correspondence with an oscillator for rapidly varying sources is retained through $D(u)$.
before.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]]. (a) $\rho$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, so $u\mapsto p(u)$ is $C^\infty$ by differentiation under the integral sign ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]]) and $p'(u)=\int y\,\rho_t(y,u)dy$; integrating by parts componentwise over a ball containing the support via the divergence theorem ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]], boundary term zero by compact support) gives $\int y_i\partial_t\rho\,dy=-\int y_i\operatorname{div}J\,dy=\int J_i\,dy$, since $\partial_i(y_iJ_k)$ contributes $J_i$ and the remaining divergence term integrates to zero. Replacing $J$ by $J_t$ (equivalently differentiating in $u$ under the integral sign) gives $p''=\int J_t$. The vanishing $\int\rho_t=0$ is the same divergence theorem with weight $1$ (equivalently clause (f) of [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]), and the total charge vanishes because $\rho$ is supported in $t\in[t_0,T]$. (b) For fixed $y\in B_a$ the one-variable function $v\mapsto J_t(y,v)$ is $C^1$ on the interval between $u$ and $u+n\cdot y/c$, whose length is at most $a/c$; the mean value theorem ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]) gives $|J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)-J_t(y,u)|\le(a/c)\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|$ componentwise, and integrating over $B_a$ with the integral triangle inequality and monotonicity ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]) gives (b). (c) Clause (b) of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] writes $E(rn,u+r/c)=E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)+$ remainder with $E_{\mathrm{lead}}=\mu_0\,n\times(n\times V(n,u))/(4\pi r)$ and remainder $O(r^{-2})$ bounded by $\Gamma_E r^{-2}$. Substituting $V=p''+(V-p'')$ and using $|n\times(n\times w)|\le|w|$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]) gives the first bound; the displayed $B$ bound is the supplier's. (d) By clause (c) of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] the limit equals $\mu_0/(16\pi^2c)\int_{S^2}|n\times V|^2d\sigma$. Replacing $V$ by $p''$ changes the integrand by at most $(2|p''|D+D^2)$ pointwise (expand $|n\times V|^2-|n\times p''|^2$ and use the bound (b), the linearity of the cross product and the integral triangle inequality), so the integral changes by at most $4\pi(2|p''|D+D^2)$ and the limit by $\mu_0(2|p''|D+D^2)/(4\pi c)$. The exact dipole value uses $|n\times p''|^2=|p''|^2-(n\cdot p'')^2$ and clause (d) of [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]]: $\int_{S^2}|n\times p''|^2d\sigma=4\pi|p''|^2-(4\pi/3)|p''|^2=(8\pi/3)|p''|^2$, and $\mu_0/(16\pi^2c)\cdot(8\pi/3)=\mu_0/(6\pi c)$. (e) records that the error coefficient $D(u)$ constrains the source's own time variation and that the limit is a fixed-retarded-time limit, as in the supplier; no self-force, point-source, decay or empirical claim is added.
before.physical_scope: Far-zone electric-dipole radiation of a prescribed smooth conserved source of compact spatial support and compact time support: the dipole moment identities, the explicit absolute dipole-replacement error $D(u)$, the uniform leading far fields and the retarded-time radiated power with its absolute error. Excluded: point charges; sources without the compact smooth branch; claims that slowness alone controls $D(u)$; observation-time power and signal-speed readings; self-force, radiation reaction and every empirical or measurement claim.

before.title: Harmonic dipole pattern and period-averaged power in the exact dipole law
before.statement: Adopt the exact dipole-law setting of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] in the long-wavelength idealization in which the transverse current moment equals the second derivative of the dipole moment ($V(n,u)=p''(u)$, i.e. $D(u)=0$), and let the dipole moment of the prescribed compact source be $p(u)=p_0\cos(\omega u)\,e_3$ with $\omega>0$, $p_0\ne0$ and $e_3$ the third basis vector (a declared model data pair, not a measured quantity; [[def-em-electric-moments]] for the moment convention). (b) [Angular power density] The retarded-time angular power density of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] is $$\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n,u)=\frac{\mu_0|n\times p''(u)|^{2}}{16\pi^{2}c}=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{16\pi^{2}c}\,\sin^{2}\theta,$$ the $\sin^{2}\theta$ pattern with zeros along $\pm e_3$ and maximum in the equatorial plane; its integral over the sphere is $$\int_{S^2}\frac{dP}{d\sigma}d\sigma=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{6\pi c},$$ using $\int_{S^2}\sin^{2}\theta\,d\sigma=8\pi/3$ from [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](a). (c) [Period average] The mean of the total power over one retarded-time period $u\in[0,2\pi/\omega]$ is $$\frac{\omega}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi/\omega}\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{6\pi c}\,du=\frac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}}{12\pi c}.$$ (d) [Scope] The computation is the exact dipole law of the model; a finite prescribed source realizes it only within the absolute error bound of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] with its $D(u)$, and a physical antenna's feed, current distribution and material realization are additional source models not supplied here. The average in (c) is taken in the retarded-time variable, not in observation time; no measurement, radiation resistance, matching condition or effective area is reported, and no empirical claim is made.
before.strategy: Direct substitution in [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]]. (a) $p(u)=p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ gives $p''(u)=-\omega^{2}p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives|the scalar multiple rule]]), and clause (c) of the theorem gives $E_{\mathrm{lead}}=\mu_0\,n\times(n\times p'')/(4\pi r)$ with $B_{\mathrm{lead}}=n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}/c$ up to the stated errors; in the exact dipole law the errors vanish. before.title: A smooth pointwise subluminal curve with no retarded root at an event
before.statement: Let $c>0$ and $a>0$, and define $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ by $z(s):=(\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}},0,0)$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[thm-of-square-roots]]). Then: (a) $z$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ and $|z'(s)|<c$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$; nevertheless there is no constant $v_*<c$ with $|z'(s)|\le v_*$ for all $s$, because $|z'(s)|\to c$ as $s\to\pm\infty$; (b) at the event $(x,t)=(0,0)$ the retarded equation $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$ of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] has no solution in $\mathbb R$: the equation reads $-s=\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}/c$, whose right-hand side is at least $a/c>0$, and squaring both sides would give $c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}=c^{2}s^{2}$, i.e. $a^{2}=0$, contrary to $a>0$. Hence pointwise subluminality of a smooth curve does not by itself produce the retarded root, and the uniform bound $v_*<c$ of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]], or an explicit cone-intersection hypothesis, cannot be dropped; the supplier [[lem-em-global-retarded-root]] indeed assumes such a uniform bound. (c) [Scope] This is a mathematical example about the prescribed curve and the root equation. The curve is future timelike pointwise ($|z'(s)|<c$ for every $s$) but not uniformly subluminal; it is not asserted to be the worldline of any physical charge, and no measurement is reported. The example contradicts no theorem: it exhibits a curve lying outside the hypotheses of the root lemma.
before.strategy: Direct verification. (a) $s\mapsto c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}$ is smooth, positive and bounded below by $a^{2}>0$, and $\sqrt\cdot$ is smooth on $(0,\infty)$; the chain rule and the derivative $\tfrac{d}{dt}\sqrt t=1/(2\sqrt t)$ give $z'(s)=(c^{2}s/\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}},0,0)$, whence $|z'(s)|=c^{2}|s|/\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}=c/\sqrt{1+a^{2}/(c^{2}s^{2})}<c$ for every $s$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[thm-of-square-roots]], [[def-abs-value]], [[lem-of-square-monotone]], algebra), while $|z'(s)|\to c$ as $s\to\infty$; so no $v_*<c$ bounds $|z'|$ on all of $\mathbb R$. (b) For $x=0$, $t=0$ the root equation of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] is $-s=|z(s)|/c=\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}/c$. Since the right-hand side is positive, $s<0$, so both sides of $-s=\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}/c$ are positive and squaring is an equivalence: it gives $c^{2}s^{2}=c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}$, i.e. $a^{2}=0$, contradicting $a>0$; alternatively, the root lemma's existence proof requires the uniform Lipschitz bound $|z(s_2)-z(s_1)|\le v_*|s_2-s_1|$ with $v_*<c$, which fails here. (c) states the scope; no physical or empirical interpretation is attached.
before.physical_scope: Mathematical example delimiting the kinematic hypothesis of the retarded point geometry: a smooth curve with $|z'|<c$ pointwise but no uniform bound, for which the retarded root equation fails at one event. Excluded: any claim about physical charges, any contradiction with theorems (the curve lies outside their hypotheses) and every empirical statement.

before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), used through the change-of-variables corollaries inside the proof of the retarded-convolution identity cited in clause (b) ([[def-countable-choice]]). The map $s:\Omega\setminus\Gamma\to\mathbb R$ is of class $C^3$, and with $R:=x-z(s)$, $r:=|R|$, $n:=R/r$, $\beta:=z'(s)/c$ and $\kappa:=1-n\cdot\beta$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]) one has $$\partial_ts(x,t)=\kappa^{-1},\qquad \nabla_xs(x,t)=-\frac{n}{c\,\kappa},\qquad \kappa\in[1-v_*/c,\,1+v_*/c],$$ so $\kappa\ge 1-v_*/c>0$ uniformly on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$. Moreover, for the fixed $x$ and near the root, the function $s'\mapsto s'+|x-z(s')|/c$ is differentiable at $s'=s$ with derivative $\kappa(x,t)$: this emission-time Jacobian $1-n\cdot\beta$ is the denominator produced by the delta substitution of clause (b).

(b) [Delta substitution and Liénard-Wiechert potentials] Let $\rho,J\in\mathcal D'(\Omega)$ be the point-source distributions of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] attached to $q$ and the worldline $z$, let $K$ be the retarded wave kernel of [[lem-em-retarded-wave-kernel]], and for $\psi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ put $(K\circledast\psi)(y,\tau):=\langle K,\psi(y+\cdot,\tau+\cdot)\rangle$ and define the retarded-history pairings by the explicit integrals $\langle\Phi,\psi\rangle:=(q/\varepsilon_0)\int_{\mathbb R}(K\circledast\psi)(z(s),s)\,ds$, $\langle\Upsilon,\psi\rangle:=\mu_0q\int_{\mathbb R}z'(s)(K\circledast\psi)(z(s),s)\,ds$, componentwise in the second case. Then these pairings are finite for every $\psi$ and their exact retarded-convolution values are $$\langle\Phi,\psi\rangle=\int_{\Omega\setminus\Gamma}\frac{C\,\psi}{\kappa\,r}\,dx\,dt,\qquad \langle\Upsilon,\psi\rangle=\int_{\Omega\setminus\Gamma}\frac{\beta}{c}\,\frac{C\,\psi}{\kappa\,r}\,dx\,dt$$ (the second identity componentwise); equivalently, $\Phi$ and $\Upsilon$ are the regular distributions of the locally integrable zero extensions to $\Gamma$ of the $C^2$ functions $\varphi:=C/(\kappa r)$ and $A:=\beta\varphi/c$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$. before.statement:
(i) [Plane-wave solutions with infinite spatial $L^2$ norm] Let $c>0$ and $W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ as in [[def-wave-equation-cauchy-data-and-wave-speed]] and [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]. For every $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ the function $u:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $u(x,t):=f(x_1-ct)$, is of class $C^\infty$ and satisfies $Wu=0$ identically. If $f\ne0$, then for every $t$ the level set $\{x:u(x,t)\ne0\}=(ct+U)\times\mathbb R^2$, where $U:=\{s\in\mathbb R:f(s)\ne0\}$ is nonempty and open, is unbounded, and $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|u(x,t)|^2\,dx=+\infty$. Consequently the smooth-data existence and smoothness clause (a) of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] carries no global finite-energy or decay conclusion: compact support of the data is a genuine hypothesis of its clause (d), not a consequence of smoothness.

(ii) [Failure of root existence without the uniform speed bound] Let $c>0$, $a>0$ and $z(s):=(\sqrt{c^2s^2+a^2},0,0)$. Then $z$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ with $|z'(s)|=\dfrac{c^2|s|}{\sqrt{c^2s^2+a^2}}<c$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$, while $\sup_{s\in\mathbb R}|z'(s)|=c$; so there is no $v_*<c$ with $|z'(s)|\le v_*$ for all $s$: the worldline is subluminal at every finite time but has no uniform subluminal bound. For the observation $(x,t)=(0,0)$ there is no root $s<t$ of $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$: the equation would read $-s=\sqrt{c^2s^2+a^2}/c$ with $s<0$, and squaring gives $s^2=s^2+a^2/c^2$, i.e. $a=0$, a contradiction. Thus the existence clause of [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]] genuinely needs its hypothesis $|z'|\le v_*<c$; the substitution denominator degenerates along this curve in the same limit.

(iii) [The event must lie off the worldline] Let $z$ be of class $C^1$ with $|z'|\le v_*<c$, and let $x=z(t)$ for some $t\in\mathbb R$. Then $s=t$ solves $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$ trivially, and the strict decrease of $s\mapsto t-s-|x-z(s)|/c$ shows that no root $s<t$ exists; hence the exclusion of the worldline $\Gamma$ in clause (a) of [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]] is a genuine hypothesis.

after.title: The proper retarded point-history pair solves the distributional wave and Maxwell equations

references.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, Cambridge lecture notes (236-page author-hosted PDF)
references.locator: Sections6.4.1–6.4.3 printed158–164 supply the potential/field background. The additional proper-history distributional wave/gauge and C1 cutoff proof is explicit here against exact library suppliers; no distributional point-source theorem is attributed to this text.

after.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let c>0, epsilon0>0, q in R, mu0=(epsilon0 c²)^-1, and let z:R->R³ be C³ with |z'(s)|<=v*<c for all s. These are mathematical parameters. On Q=R³ times R let rho,J and Phi,Upsilon be exactly the proper point-current and retarded-history distributions of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] and [[lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields]], with the kernel K of [[lem-em-retarded-wave-kernel]] and no independent free addition. Put W=c^-2 partial_t²-Delta. Then (a)
$$W\Phi=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad W\Upsilon=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}\Upsilon+c^{-2}\partial_t\Phi=0\quad\text{in }\mathcal D'(Q).$$
(b) Define the vector distributions $\mathcal E=-\nabla\Phi-\partial_t\Upsilon$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{curl}\Upsilon$ using componentwise [[def-distributional-derivative]] and the usual finite-coordinate cross/curl convention [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. They satisfy
$$\operatorname{div}\mathcal E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\quad\operatorname{div}\mathcal B=0,\quad\operatorname{curl}\mathcal E=-\partial_t\mathcal B,\quad\operatorname{curl}\mathcal B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_t\mathcal E.$$
(c) On the complement of Gamma={(z(s),s)}, these distributions restrict to the exact C1 Lienard-Wiechert fields of the earlier point-potential lemma, with all its higher-regularity branches retained. The zero extensions of those E,B formulas on Gamma belong to L1loc(Q), and their regular distributions are precisely mathcal E,mathcal B ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]). The off-worldline C1 fields also satisfy the source-free classical Maxwell equations there, because the point pair restricts to zero and each continuous regular residual is zero. Thus the equations in (b) are equations for locally integrable fields with the exact point source, not merely arbitrary field distributions. No field value on Gamma is physically assigned; zero extension is a representative convention on a null set. No physical adoption, nonlinear distribution product, finite self-energy, self-force, global acceleration bound, or incoming-field uniqueness theorem is asserted.
after.strategy:
Use only the existing explicit histories, not an undefined convolution of two noncompact distributions. Fix psi in D(Q) with observation support |x|<=M,t0<=t<=t1. The earlier point-potential proof gives a common proper-history cylinder [-S,t1] times B_L for every contributing (s,y), where S=max(0,(M+|z(0)|-ct0)/(c-v*)) and L=1+M+|z(0)|+v*max(S,|t1|); derivatives of psi have the same observation support. All relevant absolute integrals are bounded by a derivative supremum times integral over that cylinder of 1/|y|, finite by [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], with the actual nonnegative order rules [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]. If the history interval is empty all pairings vanish.
For F(y,s)=(K circledast psi)(y,s), each parameter derivative is K circledast the corresponding test derivative. Indeed on a bounded parameter neighborhood, the spatial projection of psi's support confines the kernel variable to one bounded ball; every difference quotient is dominated by its test-derivative supremum times |w|^-1 there. Dominated convergence [[thm-dominated-convergence]] and the scalar FTC show F is smooth and give those identities for all derivatives. For each fixed (y,s), translation of WK=delta from [[lem-em-retarded-wave-kernel]] yields (K circledast Wpsi)(y,s)=psi(y,s). Apply this pointwise identity inside the bounded absolute history integrals: <Phi,Wpsi>=q/epsilon0 integral psi(z(s),s)ds and <Upsilon_j,Wpsi>=mu0 q integral z'_j(s)psi(z(s),s)ds, proving the two distributional wave equations, including q0.
The function s->F(z(s),s) is C1 by [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] and has compact support in the same finite history interval: cone causality gives the upper bound, uniform subluminality gives the lower bound. Its derivative is F_s+z' dot grad_y F. Therefore the distributional Lorenz residual tested on the ORIGINAL SMOOTH psi equals
$$-\mu_0q\int_{\mathbb R}[z'(s)\cdot\nabla_yF(z(s),s)+F_s(z(s),s)]ds=0,$$
by [[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]], using c^-2/epsilon0=mu0. No derivative or cutoff is moved onto a noncompact distribution test. By [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], finite coordinate cancellations give div curl0,curl grad0 and curl curl Upsilon=grad div Upsilon-Delta Upsilon. With G=div Upsilon+c^-2 Phi_t, direct algebra gives div mathcal E=W Phi-G_t and curl mathcal B-c^-2 mathcal E_t=W Upsilon+grad G. The two wave identities and G0 prove all four equations.
Locality and local integrability. A continuous regular distribution vanishing on an open set has its function identically zero: injectivity of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] gives zero almost everywhere, and a nonzero continuous value would give a nonzero neighborhood of positive measure by [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]. Thus classical derivative compatibility below also yields the four source-free classical equations off Gamma. The earlier lemma supplies regular Phi,Upsilon and C2 potentials on Q minus Gamma. Its C1 field formulas and the classical-compatibility clause of the distributional differentiation theorem give the stated restrictions. The graph is closed and null: each fixed-time spatial section is a singleton. The Borel graph is product-measurable by [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]], and [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]] identifies product and Euclidean measure under the declared Countable Choice; hence Tonelli [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] gives zero four-dimensional measure. On any compact observation cylinder Q0, retarded s lies in [-S,t1], so A_Q=max_{[-S,t1]}|z''| is finite. With b*=v*/c, kappa>=1-b*, the explicit fields obey |E|+|B|<=C_Q(r^-2+r^-1), with constants depending on |q|,c,epsilon0,b*,A_Q, not on the individual observation point. The earlier C1 diffeomorphism g(s,y)=(z(s)+y,s+|y|/c) has absolute Jacobian kappa<=1+b*. The earlier proof establishes its global diffeomorphism property; the exact [[lem-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-borel-functions-via-radon-uniqueness]], under the declared Countable Choice, gives
$$\int_{Q_0}r^{-p}dxdt\le(1+b_*)(t_1+S)_+\int_{B_L}|y|^{-p}dy<\infty\qquad(p=1,2).$$
The last integrals are 4pi L²/2 and 4pi L respectively. Thus zero-extended classical E,B are L1loc; this alone is not yet identification across Gamma.
No hidden curve delta in the first potential derivatives. Put d=|x-z(t)|. Since t-s=r/c and |z(t)-z(s)|<=b*r, one has (1-b*)r<=d<=(1+b*)r. Potentials are consequently bounded by C/d on each compact observation cylinder. Choose a smooth spatial cutoff chi on R³, zero on B1 and one outside B2, with bounded derivative ([[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]); set chi_epsilon(x,t)=chi((x-z(t))/epsilon). This is C3, sufficient for CLASSICAL C1 integration by parts, but it need not be a C-infinity distribution test. Its spatial gradients are bounded by C/epsilon, its time derivative by Cv*/epsilon, and all are supported on epsilon<=d<=2epsilon. Ordinary compact C1 products with the original psi can be integrated by parts in each coordinate via [[thm-integration-by-parts]], followed by finite rectangle Fubini and [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] under the declared Countable Choice; equivalently extend chi_epsilon times each potential by zero, which is C1 across its vanished neighborhood. For any first spatial or time derivative D, the resulting ordinary integral identity is
$$\int \chi_\epsilon(Df)\psi=-\int \chi_\epsilon f D\psi-\int f(D\chi_\epsilon)\psi,$$
where f is any potential component off Gamma. On the cutoff shell |f|<=C/epsilon, |Dchi_epsilon|<=C'/epsilon. Spatial translations give shell volume O(epsilon³) at each t ([[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]]), and the time interval of psi is fixed; the last integral is O(epsilon). Since f and its classical first derivatives are L1loc (the latter also follow directly from the earlier D-gradient and D_t formulas with bounded compact-history acceleration), dominated convergence lets epsilon tend0 in the first two integrals. It gives -integral f Dpsi=integral (Df)psi for each ORIGINAL smooth psi. Hence global distributional first derivatives have exactly the locally integrable classical representatives, and their finite combinations identify mathcal E,mathcal B with zero-extended E,B. No product of distributions, singular-field value, stronger worldline regularity, or noncompact test action enters.

F smooth on parameter neighborhoods; F(z(s),s) has compact support and FTC gives Lorenz gauge. Commuting coordinate derivatives give four Maxwell residuals. Exact field integrability and C1 ordinary-integral cutoff Oepsilon proof identify global L1loc representatives without assigning a self-field value.

before.title: Retarded point fields off the worldline: Lienard-Wiechert potentials, the velocity/acceleration split and the uniform far-zone remainder
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the point-source change-of-variables suppliers below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]] ($c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$), let $q\in\mathbb R$ and let $z$, $v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline of a point charge, [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the constants $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), and let $\rho,J$ be the point-source distributions of that charge on the worldline in the declared point-source class of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) (the $C^3$ branch of the point-current construction). Let $(\varphi,A)$ be the retarded history pairings of [[lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields]](b) -- the framework's retarded construction for this source under the adopted selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]] -- and define $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\nabla\times A$ on the off-worldline domain $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]). Then: (a) [Potentials] $\varphi=C/(\kappa r)$ and $A=\beta\varphi/c$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, where $r,\kappa,\beta$ are the retarded data of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]](b); the zero extensions of $\varphi,A$ to $\Gamma$ are locally integrable on $\Omega$. (b) [Exact fields] On $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, $$E=E_{\mathrm{vel}}+E_{\mathrm{acc}},\qquad E_{\mathrm{vel}}=\frac{C(1-|\beta|^2)(n-\beta)}{\kappa^3r^2},\qquad E_{\mathrm{acc}}=\frac{C\,n\times\bigl((n-\beta)\times\dot\beta\bigr)}{c\,\kappa^3r},\qquad B=\frac{n\times E}{c},$$ and $E,B$ are of class $C^1$ there; the velocity part obeys $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$. before.title: Instantaneous-rest Larmor power of a prescribed point charge
before.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $q\in\mathbb R$, let $z,v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline, $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), let $s_0$ be an emission event with $z'(s_0)=0$ (the charge is momentarily at rest in the laboratory chart), and put $a:=z''(s_0)$ and, for $n\in S^2$, $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$. Let $E,B$ be the retarded fields of the charge given by [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] and $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Then: (a) [Field on the emitted sphere] For every $r>0$ and $n\in S^2$, $$E(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C\,n\times(n\times a)}{c^2r}+\rho_E(s_0,n,r),\qquad|\rho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le|C|\frac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}r^{-2},\qquad B(x_r,t_r)=\frac{n\times E(x_r,t_r)}{c}.$$ (b) [Angular flux density] The limits $$\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n):=\lim_{r\to\infty}r^2\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C^{2}\,|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}},\qquad P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\int_{S^2}\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)\,d\sigma(n),$$ exist with the convergence uniform in $n\in S^2$; $d\sigma$ is the polar surface measure of the unit sphere (equal to the chart surface measure by [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). (c) [Total power] $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\cdot\frac{8\pi}{3}|a|^{2}=\frac{q^2|a|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ the Larmor power of the momentarily resting prescribed charge. (d) [Angular distribution] Writing $\theta$ for the angle between $n$ and $a$ (with $\theta$ undefined only when $a=0$, in which case $dP/d\sigma\equiv0$), $$\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)=\frac{q^2|a|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\sin^2\theta:$$ the radiation pattern vanishes along the instantaneous acceleration axis and is maximal in the perpendicular plane; $\int_{S^2}dP/d\sigma\,d\sigma=P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$. If $a=0$ all displayed radiation quantities vanish. (e) [Scope and conventions] The result is exact at an emission event at which the charge is instantaneously at rest in the laboratory chart: then $\kappa_0(n)=1$ for every $n$, so no retarded-time conversion factor appears and the displayed limits are simultaneously the fixed-sphere flux and the emitted power per unit emission time. The item uses only the prescribed worldline and the retarded model fields -- it is not a mechanical evolution law, does not assert a self-force or radiation reaction, derives no mass, and makes no empirical or measurement claim. For a general emission event the exact formula and its low-speed comparison are the subject of the companion emitted-power theorem of this page; 'slow' motion alone is never substituted for an error bound. The prescribed curve, the uniform subluminal bound and $z'(s_0)=0$ are hypotheses; for a varying-velocity worldline the instantaneous rest event is a single parameter value, not an interval.
before.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) At the emission event $s_0$ one has $\beta_0=z'(s_0)/c=0$, $\kappa_0=1$ and $\dot\beta_0=a/c$; clause (c) of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] (equivalently clause (d) of [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]], which also supplies the uniform remainder bound and the root identification $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$) gives $E_{\mathrm{vel}}=C(1-|\beta|^2)(n-\beta)/(\kappa^3r^2)=C\,n/r^2$ and $E_{\mathrm{acc}}=C\,n\times((n-\beta)\times\dot\beta)/(c\kappa^3r)=C\,n\times(n\times a)/(c^2r)$; the displayed remainder is their sum restricted to the leading term, bounded by $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$; $B=n\times E/c$. (b) For fields with $B=n\times E/c$ one has $n\cdot S=n\cdot(E\times B)/\mu_0=(|E|^2-(n\cdot E)^2)/(\mu_0c)=|n\times E|^2/(\mu_0c)$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). Hence $r^2n\cdot S=r^2|n\times E|^2/(\mu_0c)$; replacing $E=E_{\mathrm{lead}}+\rho_E$ and using the bound on $\rho_E$ together with $|n\times w|\le|w|$ gives $r^2n\cdot S=C^{2}|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})+O(r^{-1})$ uniformly on $S^2$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]); integrating over the compact sphere and passing to the limit ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]) proves the limits and their uniformity. (c) Expand $|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}=|a|^{2}-(n\cdot a)^{2}$ and apply [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d): $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$, so the integral is $4\pi|a|^2-(4\pi/3)|a|^2=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$; with $C^2=q^2/(16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2)$ and $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$ the coefficient is $C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})\cdot(8\pi/3)=q^2/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$. (d) The vanishing of the pattern along $\pm a$ and the value $\sin^2\theta$ follow from $n\times(n\times a)=n(n\cdot a)-a$ and $|\cdot|^2=|a|^2\cos^2\theta-2|a|^2\cos^2\theta+|a|^2=|a|^2\sin^2\theta$; the displayed coefficient is $C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})=q^{2}/(16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ by the same unit relation. The integral statement is (c). (e) At $\beta_0=0$ the emission-time Jacobian $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot\beta_0$ equals $1$ for all $n$, so the retarded-time conversion factor is trivial and the fixed-sphere flux limit is the emitted power per unit emission time ([[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]](a) for the Jacobian); the scope exclusions are those of the point-field supplier, and no mechanical, self-force or empirical conclusion is drawn.

before.title: Relativistic emitted power of a prescribed point charge at a general emission event
before.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the setting be that of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]]: a charge $q\in\mathbb R$ ($C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$) on a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline $z$ in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], with retarded fields $E,B$ off the worldline and the uniform far-zone remainder of that item; let $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]). Let $s_0$ be an emission event, $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\gamma_0:=(1-|\beta_0|^2)^{-1/2}$, $a:=z''(s_0)$, and for $n\in S^2$ put $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$, $\kappa_0(n):=1-n\cdot\beta_0$. Define the **emitted power at the emission event $s_0$** by the $\kappa_0$-weighted far-zone flux $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}\kappa_0(n)\,r^{2}\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)\,d\sigma(n),$$ $d\sigma$ the polar surface measure (equal to the chart surface measure). The weight $\kappa_0$ is the emission-time/observation-time conversion factor of the retarded root, $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$, equivalently the moving-boundary correction $S\cdot n-(z'\cdot n)u$ at leading radiation order, where $u=|S|/c$ for the transverse far field. Then: (a) [Weighted flux limit] The limit exists and $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\int_{S^2}\frac{\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}}{\kappa_0(n)^{5}}\,d\sigma(n).$$ (b) [Closed form and four-acceleration form] If $b:=|\beta_0|<1$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp$ is decomposed along $\beta_0=|\beta_0|e_3$ and perpendicular to it, then $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{q^{2}\gamma_0^{6}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\bigl(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}\bigr)=\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\,\eta(A,A),$$ where $A$ is the four-acceleration of the worldline at $s_0$ and $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](e)). At $\beta_0=0$ the weight is $1$ and (b) reduces to the instantaneous-rest Larmor power of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]]. (c) [Low-speed comparison] For every $\delta\in(0,1)$ and every emission event with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$, $$\frac{(1-\delta^{2})^{-2}q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)\le\frac{(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},\qquad\text{hence}\qquad \Bigl|P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)-\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\Bigr|\le\frac{3\delta^{2}}{(1-\delta^{2})^{3}}\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ a comparison uniform over the events with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. In particular the instantaneous-rest formula is the exact $\delta=0$ case, and no term of the comparison is asserted to be small without the explicit hypothesis $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. (d) [Scope] $P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$ is the power emitted at the single retarded event $s_0$ per unit emission time, defined by the weighted far-zone flux; it is not a coordinate-time loss rate of a dynamical particle, and no dynamics (self-force, radiation reaction, mass), no uniformity in $s_0$, and no empirical or measurement claim is made. The near fields are $O(r^{-2})$ with their uniform remainder as in [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]](c), so their contribution to the weighted $r^2$ flux vanishes; the $\kappa_0$-weighting is part of the definition of emitted power and is not an additional physical assumption.
before.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) On the emitted sphere the retarded data are those of the emission event ($s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]](d)), and the uniform remainder gives $E= E_{\mathrm{acc,lead}}+\rho_E$ with $E_{\mathrm{acc,lead}}=C\,n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)/(c\kappa_0^{3}r)$, $|\rho_E|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$ and $B=n\times E/c$. For such fields $n\cdot S=|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)$ (expand $E\times(n\times E/c)$ and use the triple-product orthogonality, [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Therefore $\kappa_0r^{2}n\cdot S=\kappa_0r^{2}|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)=\kappa_0|C|^{2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{3}\kappa_0^{6})+O(r^{-1})$ with a remainder controlled by the uniform bound ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]); note $C^{2}=|C|^{2}$ as squares. Integrating over the compact sphere and passing to the limit ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]) gives (a) with $\dot\beta_0=a/c$ absorbed: $|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}$ replaces $c^{2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)|^{2}$, giving $(C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5}))\int|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}/\kappa_0^{5}d\sigma$ because $|C|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{3}c^{2})=C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})$ and one power of $\kappa_0$ cancels. (b) Rotate the integration variable so that $\beta_0=be_3$ with $b=|\beta_0|$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp e_1$ (rotation invariance of $\sigma$, [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]); put $u=n_3$ and $\kappa_0=1-bu$. Expanding the numerator with $N=n\cdot\beta_0=bu$, $d=n\cdot\dot\beta_0$ and $|n-\beta_0|^{2}=1-2bu+b^{2}$ gives, exactly as in the recorded research computation, $$\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}=-(1-b^{2})(n\cdot a)^{2}+2\kappa_0 b\,a_\parallel(n\cdot a)+\kappa_0^{2}|a|^{2}.$$ Apply [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](b),(c) with $f(u)=(1-bu)^{-5}$ and $g(u)=(1-bu)^{-4}$: the azimuthal average turns $(n\cdot a)^2$ into $u^{2}a_\parallel^{2}+\tfrac12(1-u^{2})a_\perp^{2}$ and $n\cdot a$ into $ua_\parallel$, and $(1-bu)^{-3}$ weights the $|a|^{2}$ term. The resulting one-dimensional integrals are elementary: $\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})(1-bu)^{-5}du=\tfrac{4}{3}(1-b^{2})^{-3}$ and $\int_{-1}^{1}(1-bu)^{-3}du=2(1-b^{2})^{-2}$, both verified by the displayed antiderivatives in $y=1-bu$ using the power derivative, chain rule and fundamental theorem ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). Collecting terms gives $\int|\cdot|^{2}/\kappa_0^{5}d\sigma=(8\pi/3)[\gamma_0^{6}a_\parallel^{2}+\gamma_0^{4}a_\perp^{2}]= (8\pi/3)\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$; multiplying by $C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})=q^{2}/(16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ produces (b). The four-acceleration identity is clause (e) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]], where $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_w^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_w^{6}(w\cdot a)^{2}/c^{2}$ with $w=z'(s_0)=c\beta_0$ reads $\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$; the $\beta_0=0$ case is the statement of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]]. (c) From (b), $\gamma_0^{6}= (1-|\beta_0|^{2})^{-3}\le(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}$ and $|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}\ge(1-|\beta_0|^{2})|a|^{2}\ge(1-\delta^{2})|a|^{2}$ give the lower bound $\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})\ge(1-\delta^{2})^{-2}|a|^{2}$; the upper bound is $\gamma_0^{6}|a|^{2}\le(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}|a|^{2}$. The displayed difference bound uses $(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}-1\le3\delta^{2}(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}$ and $1-(1-\delta^{2})^{-2}\le3\delta^{2}(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}$ for $0<\delta<1$ (elementary rational inequalities on $\delta^{2}\in(0,1)$). (d) records that the definition is per unit emission time, that the near-field contribution vanishes after weighting by the uniform remainder and that no dynamics or empirical content is added.
before.physical_scope: Emitted power per unit emission time of a prescribed point charge at a general emission event on a uniformly subluminal $C^3$ worldline: the $\kappa$-weighted far-zone flux, the closed form $q^2\gamma^6(|a|^2-|\beta\times a|^2)/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^3)=q^2\eta(A,A)/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^3)$ and the uniform $\delta$-comparison with the instantaneous-rest Larmor value. Excluded: dynamical evolution, self-force, radiation reaction, mass derivation, coordinate-time loss rates, uniformity in the emission event and every empirical or measurement claim.

before.title: Self-force, runaways and finite-size regularizations are not supplied by this page
before.statement: Record, with no speculative content, the limits of the radiation model built on this page. (a) [Self-energy] The truncated field energy of the idealized point charge diverges as the inner cutoff is removed ([[pthm-em-point-self-energy-divergence]]): the point source's own field carries infinite energy in this framework's idealization, and any finite-energy treatment of a point-like charge requires modifying the source or the field near the singularity, or an explicit cutoff, none of which is supplied here. (b) [Undefined self-interaction] The framework's source model [[def-em-weak-sources]] pairs distributions against compact smooth tests and expressly excludes arbitrary products of distributions; the point charge's field is singular on the worldline while its own current is a distribution supported there, so the pairing of the charge's own field with its own current -- the object a systematic self-force would have to use -- is not defined by these postulates, no regularization is adopted, and no equation of motion for the charge is derived. (c) [What the emitted-power items do and do not give] [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]] and [[pthm-em-lienard-emitted-power]] are prescribed-source statements: they compute the emitted power of a stipulated worldline at a stipulated emission event and determine no worldline evolution, no back-reaction and no coordinate-time rate; they are not a mechanical model. (d) [Deferred, not claimed] Extended-charge or finite-size regularizations of the self-field, the well-posedness of any self-force dynamics, runaway solutions and an electromagnetic derivation of rest mass are outside this page and are neither stated nor proved here. No experiment, measurement, statistical estimate or precision is reported or implied, and nothing in this remark is a refutation of any physical theory.
before.strategy: A scope remark: no proof is claimed and the item is reviewed for formulation and scope only. The review checks that (i) the divergence statement is exactly the cited theorem's idealization and is not upgraded into a claim that a physical particle has infinite energy ([pthm-em-point-self-energy-divergence](c) makes that reading explicit); (ii) the product of distributions is correctly identified as undefined in the declared model [[def-em-weak-sources]], so no self-force expression is written down; (iii) the emitted-power theorems are quoted at their exact prescribed-source scope, with observation-time versus emission-time distinctions preserved; and (iv) the deferred list names what is genuinely absent instead of asserting a speculative result. No empirical content is introduced.

before.title: Conditional radius loss of a prescribed slowly orbiting charge in a reduced quasistatic model
before.statement: Adopt the following idealized, hypothetical setup of a prescribed slowly orbiting charge; it is a thought experiment with explicit premises, not a reported measurement. (H) Let $m>0$ be an externally supplied rest mass and $q\ne0$ a charge parameter ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]), let $\kappa>0$, and let the particle move on a circle of radius $r(t)>0$ about a fixed centre in the laboratory chart ([[def-em-lab-geometry]]) so that the mechanical orbit is governed by the attractive potential $V(r)=-\kappa/r$: the circular-orbit energy is $E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r)=-\kappa/(2r)$ and the circular orbit with speed $v$ satisfies $mv^{2}=\kappa/r$, with centripetal acceleration $a=\kappa/(mr^{2})$. Assume the adiabatic separation of timescales: the mechanical parameters change on a timescale long compared with the orbital period, the speed is small compared with $c$, and the electromagnetic energy emitted per unit time is instantaneously taken to be the Larmor value $q^{2}a(t)^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]] evaluated at the instantaneous centripetal acceleration, so that the adopted energy balance of the reduced model reads $$\frac{d}{dt}E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r(t))=-\frac{q^{2}a(t)^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}.$$ Then, with $A:=q^{2}\kappa/(3\pi\varepsilon_0m^{2}c^{3})>0$: (a) the reduced model implies $r'(t)=-A/r(t)^{2}$ for all $t$ where the model applies, and the circular orbit radius in the reduced model obeys $$r(t)^{3}=r_{0}^{3}-3A(t-t_{0})$$ on any interval containing $t_0$ on which $r>0$; (b) consequently $r$ is strictly decreasing, and the cubic reaches $r=0$ at the finite reduced-model time $t_{*}:=t_{0}+r_{0}^{3}/(3A)$, with $r(t)\downarrow0$ as $t\uparrow t_{*}$; (c) [Scope and qualifications] the deduction is conditional on (H). The low-speed premise $v^{2}=\kappa/(mr)\ll c^{2}$ necessarily fails as $r\to0$, so the model's own hypotheses break down near the collapse time and the computation is not a proof that a physical orbit reaches $r=0$; it is not a derivation of atomic lifetimes, not a coupled point-particle self-force calculation (that dynamics is not available in this framework), and it supplies no empirical evidence. The reduced-model finite-time collapse is retained as a mathematical property of (H), while all conclusions about nature remain conditional on (H) and on its regime of validity. No measurement, dataset, statistical model or uncertainty is introduced.
before.strategy: A complete conditional deduction from (H). (a) Differentiate $E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r)=-\kappa/(2r)$ along $r(t)$: the power rule gives $\tfrac{d}{dt}(-\kappa/(2r))=\kappa r'/(2r^{2})$ ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]); the balance (H) reads $\kappa r'/(2r^{2})=-q^{2}a^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$; substituting $a=\kappa/(mr^{2})$ and solving for $r'$ gives $r'=-q^{2}\kappa/(3\pi\varepsilon_0m^{2}c^{3}r^{2})=-A/r^{2}$. Multiplying by $3r^{2}$ gives $\tfrac{d}{dt}(r^{3})=-3A$, and the fundamental theorem applied on any interval where $r>0$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[def-interval]]) yields the displayed cubic; equivalently, differentiating the cubic reproduces the ODE, so the two are equivalent in the reduced model. (b) $r'=-A/r^{2}<0$ since $A>0$, so $r$ is strictly decreasing wherever the model applies; from the cubic, $r(t)^{3}\downarrow0$ as $t\uparrow t_{*}=t_{0}+r_{0}^{3}/(3A)$, and $r(t)^{3}<0$ beyond $t_{*}$ records the breakdown rather than a negative radius. (c) The scope clause records the failure of $v^{2}=\kappa/(mr)\ll c^{2}$ as $r\to0$, the absence of any coupled self-force dynamics in the framework (the point self-field is singular and its product with the current is undefined, as recorded by the scope remark on this page), and the absence of empirical content: this is a mapped, reduced model with a finite-time formal collapse, exactly as stated, and the conclusion is conditional on (H) throughout. No new physical mechanism is postulated and the Larmor input is cited at its exact instantaneously-rest hypothesis; the adiabatic and low-speed premises are part of (H), not derived.
before.physical_scope: Reduced quasistatic circular-orbit model with an adopted Larmor energy-balance premise (H): the radius ODE $r'=-A/r^{2}$, the cubic solution $r^{3}=r_{0}^{3}-3A(t-t_{0})$ and the formal finite-time collapse limit as a property of (H). Excluded: any claim that a physical orbit reaches the centre or an atom decays in finite time; coupled self-force dynamics; derivation of lifetimes; measurements, statistical models and every empirical claim.
